title.zh: 卷三百三十六 列傳第九十五 司馬光子:康 呂公著子:希哲 希純
title.en: Volume 336 Biographies 95: Sima Guang and Sons:Kang, Lu Gongzhe and Son: Xizhe, Xi Chun
title.raw: 卷三百三十六 列傳第九十五 司馬光子:康 呂公著子:希哲 希純 Volume 336 Biographies 95: Sima Guang and Sons:Kang, Lu Gongzhe and Son: Xizhe, Xi Chun

sentences.zh: 司馬光

translations.literal: Sima Guang
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 司馬光，字君實，陝州夏縣人也。

translations.literal: Sima Guang, styled Junshi, was a native of Xia County in Shaan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang, whose courtesy name was Junshi, came from Xia County in Shaan Province.

sentences.zh: 父池，天章閣待制。

translations.literal: His father Chi was a Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi served as a Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.

sentences.zh: 光生七歲，凜然如成人，聞講《左氏春秋》，愛之，退為家人講，即了其大指。

translations.literal: Guang was born; at age seven he was stern as an adult. Hearing lectures on the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, he loved it; returning home he lectured his family on it and at once understood its main purport.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang was seven, he carried himself with the gravity of a grown man. After hearing the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals taught, he took to it at once; back at home he explained it to his household and immediately grasped its larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 自是手不釋書，至不知饑渴寒暑。

translations.literal: From then on his hand never left his books, to the point that he did not notice hunger, thirst, cold, or heat.
translations.idiomatic: From that time he scarcely set his books aside, so absorbed that he scarcely noticed hunger, thirst, or the change of seasons.

sentences.zh: 群兒戲于庭，一兒登甕，足跌沒水中，眾皆棄去，光持石擊甕破之，水迸，兒得活。

translations.literal: The neighborhood boys were playing in the courtyard; one boy climbed onto a jar, his foot slipped and he fell into the water. All fled, but Guang took a stone and smashed the jar; the water burst forth and the boy lived.
translations.idiomatic: While the neighborhood children were playing in the courtyard, one boy climbed onto a large jar, slipped, and fell into the water inside. Everyone else ran away, but Guang picked up a stone, broke the jar, and let the water rush out so the boy could live.

sentences.zh: 其後京、洛間畫以為圖。

translations.literal: Afterward in the capital region pictures of this were made.
translations.idiomatic: Later the story was painted in pictures throughout the capital region.

sentences.zh: 仁宗寶元初，中進士甲科。

translations.literal: In the early Baoyuan era of Emperor Renzong he passed the jinshi examination in the first class.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Baoyuan reign of Emperor Renzong he placed in the top tier of the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 年甫冠，性不喜華靡，聞喜宴獨不戴花，同列語之曰：「君賜不可違。」

translations.literal: He had just reached manhood; by nature he disliked luxury and extravagance. At the celebratory banquet he alone did not wear the ceremonial flower. His fellows said to him: "The sovereign's gift may not be refused."
translations.idiomatic: He had only just come of age and by temperament disliked ostentation. At the victory banquet for successful candidates he alone refused the customary floral ornament. His companions told him, "You cannot refuse what the sovereign bestows."

sentences.zh: 乃簪一枝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pinned on a single spray.
translations.idiomatic: So he pinned on a single blossom.

sentences.zh: 除奉禮郎，時池在杭，求簽蘇州判官事以便親，許之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman for Ceremonial Observance. At the time his father Chi was in Hangzhou; he requested an appointment as assayer in Suzhou to be near his parent, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as Gentleman for Ceremonial Observance. His father Chi was then serving in Hangzhou, and Guang asked to be posted as assayer in Suzhou so he could be close to him; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 丁內外艱，執喪累年，毀瘠如禮。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for the deaths of both parents, keeping vigil for several years and becoming emaciated in accordance with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When both parents died he observed the full mourning rites for years, wasting away in the manner prescribed by ritual.

sentences.zh: 服除，簽書武成軍判官事，改大理評事，補國子直講。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed noting clerk of the Wucheng Army, then promoted to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and supplemented as lecturer in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made noting clerk of the Wucheng Army, then promoted to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and given a supplementary post as lecturer in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 樞密副使龐籍薦為館閣校勘，同知禮院。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pang Ji recommended him as collator in the Hall of Literature and concurrent director of the Court of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Pang Ji of the Bureau of Military Affairs recommended him for collator in the Hall of Literature and concurrent director of the Court of Rites.

sentences.zh: 中官麥允言死，給鹵簿。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Mai Yunyan died, he was granted imperial funeral regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Mai Yunyan died, the court granted him imperial funeral regalia.

sentences.zh: 光言：「繁纓以朝，孔子且猶不可。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Ornate cap tassels worn at court — even Confucius would not have approved.
translations.idiomatic: Guang objected: "Ornate cap tassels in court dress — even Confucius regarded that as improper.

sentences.zh: 允言近習之臣，非有元勳大勞而贈以三公官，給一品鹵簿，其視繁纓，不亦大乎！」

translations.literal: Yunyan was a favorite close attendant; he had no founding achievement or great service, yet was posthumously granted the rank of a Three Dukes and given first-rank funeral regalia — compared with ornate tassels, is this not far worse!"
translations.idiomatic: Yunyan was merely a favored intimate of the throne, with no signal merit to his name, yet they would ennoble him posthumously to the rank of a Three Dukes and award first-rank funeral regalia — is that not a far graver breach than ornate tassels?"

sentences.zh: 夏竦賜諡「文正」，光言：「此諡之至美者，竦何人，可以當之？」

translations.literal: Xia Song was granted the posthumous epithet "Cultured and Correct"; Guang said: "This is the most exalted epithet — what sort of man is Song that he could bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Song was given the posthumous epithet Cultured and Correct, Guang protested: "That epithet is the highest honor — what has Song done to deserve it?"

sentences.zh: 改「文莊」。

translations.literal: It was changed to "Cultured and Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: The epithet was changed to "Cultured and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 加集賢校理。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 從龐籍辟，通判并州。

translations.literal: Following Pang Ji he entered his staff and was made vice prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Pang Ji's staff and was appointed vice prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 麟州屈野河西多良田，夏人蠶食其地，為河東患。

translations.literal: West of the Quye River in Linzhou there was much fertile land; the Western Xia nibbled away at it, becoming a scourge to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Quye River in Linzhou lay rich farmland that the Western Xia were encroaching upon, to the great distress of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 籍命光按視，光建：「築二堡以制夏人，募民耕之，耕者眾則糴賤，亦可漸紓河東貴糴遠輸之憂。」

translations.literal: Ji ordered Guang to inspect on site. Guang proposed: "Build two forts to restrain the Western Xia, recruit civilians to farm there — if many farm, grain will be cheap, and this can gradually ease Hedong's worry over costly grain and distant transport."
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent Guang to survey the ground. Guang recommended: "Erect two fortified posts to check the Western Xia and recruit settlers to farm the land. Once many are farming, grain prices will fall, and that will gradually relieve Hedong's burden of dear grain hauled from afar."

sentences.zh: 籍從其策；

translations.literal: Ji followed his plan;
translations.idiomatic: Ji adopted his plan;

sentences.zh: 而麟將郭恩勇且狂，引兵夜渡河，不設備，沒於敵，籍得罪去。

translations.literal: but the Linzhou general Guo En was brave yet reckless; he led troops across the river by night without taking precautions and perished at the enemy's hands, and Ji was punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: but the Linzhou commander Guo En, bold to the point of rashness, led his men across the river by night without proper precautions and was wiped out by the enemy; Ji was blamed and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 光三上書自引咎，不報。

translations.literal: Guang submitted three memorials taking blame upon himself; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Guang three times memorialized the throne accepting blame himself, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 籍沒，光升堂拜其妻如母，撫其子如昆弟，時人賢之。

translations.literal: When Ji died, Guang entered the hall and bowed to his wife as to a mother, and treated his sons as younger brothers; men of the time praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji's death Guang went to his home, paid obeisance to his widow as to a mother, and cared for his sons as he would younger brothers — conduct the age admired.

sentences.zh: 改直秘閣、開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to direct access to the Secret Repository and investigating censor of the Kaifeng prefectural court.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as having direct access to the Secret Repository and as investigating censor in the Kaifeng prefectural court.

sentences.zh: 交趾貢異獸，謂之麟，光言：「真偽不可知，使其真，非自至不足為瑞，願還其獻。」

translations.literal: Jiaozhi presented a strange beast called a qilin. Guang said: "Whether it is genuine cannot be known; even if genuine, if it did not come of itself it is no auspicious sign — I ask that the tribute be returned."
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi sent tribute of a strange creature called a qilin. Guang argued: "We cannot even tell whether it is real; and if it were, a beast that did not arrive unbidden is no true portent. I urge that the tribute be sent back."

sentences.zh: 又奏賦以風。

translations.literal: He also submitted a fu-rhapsody as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a fu-rhapsody by way of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 修起居注，判禮部。

translations.literal: He compiled the Veritable Records and concurrently judged the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of compiling the Veritable Records and concurrently served as judge of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 有司奏日當食，故事食不滿分，或京師不見，皆表賀。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported that the sun would be eclipsed; by precedent when the eclipse was incomplete, or when it was not visible in the capital, all submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported an impending solar eclipse; by precedent, if the eclipse was partial, or if it could not be seen in the capital, officials all submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 光言：「四方見，京師不見，此人君為陰邪所蔽；

translations.literal: Guang said: "If it is seen in the four quarters but not in the capital, this means the ruler is obscured by yin and perverse forces;
translations.idiomatic: Guang objected: "When the eclipse is visible throughout the realm but not in the capital, it means the Son of Heaven is overshadowed by dark and corrupt influences;

sentences.zh: 天下皆知而朝廷獨不知，其為災當益甚，不當賀。」

translations.literal: the whole world knows yet the court alone does not — the calamity should be all the worse; one ought not congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: everyone under Heaven knows while the court alone does not — the omen is only more grave, and congratulations are out of place."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 同知諫院。

translations.literal: Concurrent director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was made concurrent director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 蘇轍答制策切直，考官胡宿將黜之，光言：「轍有愛君憂國之心，不宜黜。」

translations.literal: Su Zhe's answers to the policy examination were sharp and direct; the examiner Hu Su was about to fail him. Guang said: "Zhe has a heart that loves the ruler and grieves for the state — he should not be failed."
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe's policy examination answers were blunt and forthright; the examiner Hu Su was about to fail him. Guang said: "Zhe shows a loyal concern for ruler and realm; he should not be failed."

sentences.zh: 詔置末級。

translations.literal: An edict placed him in the lowest rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed him at the bottom of the pass list.

sentences.zh: 仁宗始不豫，國嗣未立，天下寒心而莫敢言。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong first fell ill; the heir to the state was not established; all under Heaven were anxious yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong first fell ill and no heir had been named, the empire held its breath, yet no one dared speak openly.

sentences.zh: 諫官范鎮首發其議，光在并州聞而繼之，且貽書勸鎮以死爭。

translations.literal: The remonstrance official Fan Zhen first raised the issue; Guang, hearing of it in Bingzhou, followed with his own memorial and also sent a letter urging Zhen to contend even at the cost of his life.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrator Fan Zhen was first to broach the matter; Guang, hearing of it while serving in Bingzhou, followed with his own memorial and wrote urging Zhen to press the point even at the risk of death.

sentences.zh: 至是，復面言：「臣昔通判并州，所上三章，願陛下果斷力行。」

translations.literal: By then he again spoke to the throne in person: "Your servant once served as vice prefect of Bingzhou and submitted three memorials on this; I pray Your Majesty will act decisively and carry them through."
translations.idiomatic: Now he spoke again in person: "When I was vice prefect of Bingzhou I submitted three memorials on this; I beg Your Majesty to act with resolution and see them through."

sentences.zh: 帝沉思久之，曰：「得非欲選宗室為繼嗣者乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor pondered long and said: "Do you not wish to select someone from the imperial clan as successor?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fell silent a long while, then said: "Are you not asking me to choose an heir from among the imperial clan?

sentences.zh: 此忠臣之言，但人不敢及耳。」

translations.literal: This is the speech of a loyal minister — only no one dares say it."
translations.idiomatic: That is the counsel of a loyal minister — it is only that no one else dares utter it."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「臣言此，自謂必死，不意陛下開納。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "Your servant spoke thus expecting surely to die; I did not expect Your Majesty to receive it openly."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "When I spoke thus I expected to die for it; I never dreamed Your Majesty would hear me with such openness."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此何害，古今皆有之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What harm is there? Such things have occurred in antiquity and in the present."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "What harm is there in that? Rulers ancient and modern have done the same."

sentences.zh: 光退未聞命，復上疏曰：「臣向者進說，意謂即行，今寂無所聞，此必有小人言陛下春秋鼎盛，何遽為不祥之事。

translations.literal: Guang withdrew without hearing a decision; he submitted another memorial: "Your servant's earlier advice was meant to be carried out at once; now all is silent — surely petty men are telling Your Majesty that you are in the prime of life and asking why you would broach so inauspicious a matter.
translations.idiomatic: Guang withdrew without receiving orders, then memorialized again: "I meant my earlier counsel to be acted on immediately; now nothing is heard — surely petty men are saying Your Majesty is in the prime of life and asking why you would raise so ill-omened a topic.

sentences.zh: 小人無遠慮，特欲倉卒之際，援立其所厚善者耳。

translations.literal: Petty men lack far-sightedness; they only wish, in a sudden crisis, to install someone they have long favored.
translations.idiomatic: Such men lack foresight; they only want, when crisis comes in haste, to put on the throne whomever they have long favored.

sentences.zh: 『定策國老』、『門生天子』之禍，可勝言哉？」

translations.literal: The disasters of "the elder who fixed the succession" and "the emperor who was his disciple's creature" — can they be told in full?"
translations.idiomatic: The catastrophes of "the elder statesman who fixed the succession" and "the Son of Heaven who was his pupil's creature" — need I recount them at length?"

sentences.zh: 帝大感動曰：「送中書。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply moved and said: "Send this to the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the Emperor said: "Send this to the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 光見韓琦等曰：「諸公不及今定議，異日禁中夜半出寸紙，以某人為嗣，則天下莫敢違。」

translations.literal: Guang saw Han Qi and the others and said: "If you gentlemen do not settle this now, someday in the dead of night the palace will issue a scrap of paper naming someone as heir, and none under Heaven will dare disobey."
translations.idiomatic: Guang told Han Qi and the others: "Unless you settle the succession now, one night the palace will issue a slip of paper naming an heir, and the whole realm will have no choice but to obey."

sentences.zh: 琦等拱手曰：「敢不盡力。」

translations.literal: Qi and the others bowed with clasped hands and said: "We dare not fail to do our utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Qi and the others bowed with folded hands: "We shall spare no effort."

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔英宗判宗正，辭不就，遂立為皇子，又稱疾不入。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Yingzong to administer the Imperial Clan Court; he declined and would not take the post; then he was established as imperial son, yet again pleaded illness and would not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict named Yingzong to head the Imperial Clan Court; he declined and would not accept. He was then named imperial son, yet again pleaded illness and refused to enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 光言：「皇子辭不貲之富，至於旬月，其賢於人遠矣。

translations.literal: Guang said: "The imperial son has declined unearned wealth for as much as ten days — his virtue far surpasses other men.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "The prince has refused unearned riches for a month and more — his virtue already sets him far above ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 然父召無諾，君命召不俟駕，願以臣子大義責皇子，宜必入。」

translations.literal: Yet when a father summons there is no answering "no"; when the ruler's command comes one does not wait to harness the chariot — I pray that by the great duty of subject and son the prince be compelled; he is sure to enter."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when a father calls, a son does not refuse; when the sovereign commands, a subject does not wait to yoke his carriage. I urge that the prince be pressed by the great obligations of son and subject — then he will surely come."

sentences.zh: 英宗遂受命。

translations.literal: Yingzong thereupon accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong then accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 兗國公主嫁李瑋，不相能，詔出瑋衛州，母楊歸其兄璋，主入居禁中。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yan'guo was married to Li Wei; they could not get along. An edict sent Wei out to Weizhou; the mother Yang was returned to her brother Zhang; the princess entered the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yan'guo was married to Li Wei, but the two could not live together. An edict banished Wei to Weizhou, sent the mother Yang back to her brother Zhang, and had the princess take up residence in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 光言：「陛下追念章懿太后，故使瑋尚主。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Your Majesty, recalling Empress Dowager Zhangyi, therefore had Wei marry the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "Your Majesty, remembering Empress Dowager Zhangyi, gave Wei the princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 今乃母子離析，家事流落，獨無雨露之感乎？

translations.literal: Now mother and son are torn apart and the family's affairs are scattered — have you no feeling of imperial grace and compassion?
translations.idiomatic: Now mother and son are separated and the household is broken up — is there no room for gracious compassion?

sentences.zh: 瑋既黜，主安得無罪？」

translations.literal: Since Wei has been dismissed, how can the princess be without fault?"
translations.idiomatic: If Wei is punished, can the princess be held blameless?"

sentences.zh: 帝悟，降主沂國，待李氏恩不衰。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood; the princess was demoted to Princess of Yi'guo, and the Li family continued to receive favor undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took his point; the princess was demoted to Princess of Yi'guo, while the Li family continued to enjoy undiminished favor.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥，固辭，改天章閣待制兼侍講、知諫院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to drafter of edicts but firmly declined; he was changed to Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, concurrently lecturer and director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to drafter of edicts, he firmly declined; he was instead made Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, with concurrent posts as lecturer and director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時朝政頗姑息，胥史諠譁則逐中執法，輦官悖慢則退宰相，衛士凶逆而獄不窮治，軍卒詈三司使而以為非犯階級。

translations.literal: At the time court governance was quite indulgent: when clerks made an uproar the middle-ranking law enforcer was expelled; when palace attendants were insolent the chief minister was dismissed; when guards committed violence the case was not thoroughly investigated; when soldiers cursed the Commissioner of the Three Departments it was treated as not violating hierarchy.
translations.idiomatic: Court governance had grown indulgent: when clerks raised a clamor the middle law officer was dismissed; when palace attendants were rude the chief minister was removed; when guards committed outrage the case was not fully pursued; when soldiers reviled the Commissioner of the Three Departments it was deemed no breach of rank.

sentences.zh: 光言皆陵遲之漸，不可以不正。

translations.literal: Guang said these were all signs of decline and could not be left uncorrected.
translations.idiomatic: Guang warned that each was a step toward decline and could not be left unchecked.

sentences.zh: 充媛董氏薨，贈淑妃，輟朝成服，百官奉慰，定諡，行冊禮，葬給鹵簿。

translations.literal: The Gentle Lady Dong died and was posthumously made Imperial Concubine; the court suspended audiences and donned mourning; officials offered condolences; an epithet was fixed; investiture rites were performed; burial was granted imperial funeral regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When Gentle Lady Dong died she was posthumously made Imperial Concubine; the court suspended audiences and wore mourning; officials offered condolences; an epithet was granted; investiture rites were held; and imperial funeral regalia was provided for the burial.

sentences.zh: 光言：「董氏秩本微，病革方拜充媛。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Lady Dong's rank was originally low; only when gravely ill was she made Gentle Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Guang objected: "Lady Dong's rank was humble to begin with; only on her deathbed was she made Gentle Lady.

sentences.zh: 古者婦人無諡，近制惟皇后有之。

translations.literal: In antiquity women had no posthumous epithets; in recent regulations only the empress did.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity women received no posthumous epithets; under recent rules only an empress did.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿本以賞軍功，未嘗施於婦人。

translations.literal: Funeral regalia was originally to reward military achievement and was never applied to women.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial funeral regalia was meant to reward military merit and had never been extended to women.

sentences.zh: 唐平陽公主有舉兵佐高祖定天下功，乃得給。

translations.literal: Only the Princess of Pingyang of Tang, for raising troops to help Gaozu settle the realm, received it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tang's Princess of Pingyang, who raised forces to help Gaozu secure the empire, had been granted such honors.

sentences.zh: 至韋庶人始令妃主葬日皆給鼓吹，非令典，不足法。」

translations.literal: It was under Empress Wei that consorts and princesses were first given martial music at burial — not a proper precedent and not to be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Only under Empress Wei were consorts and princesses first given martial music at burial — a corrupt precedent, not to be imitated."

sentences.zh: 時有司定後宮封贈法，后與妃俱贈三代，光論：「妃不當與后同，袁盎引卻慎夫人席，正為此耳。

translations.literal: At the time the relevant offices were fixing regulations for posthumous ennoblement in the inner palace; empress and consort alike were to ennoble three generations of forebears. Guang argued: "A consort should not be the same as an empress — Yuan Ang moved Lady Shen from her seat for just this reason.
translations.idiomatic: While offices were drafting rules for posthumous honors in the inner palace — empress and consort alike ennobling three generations — Guang argued: "A consort must not rank with an empress; Yuan Ang had Lady Shen's seat moved back for exactly this reason.

sentences.zh: 天聖親郊，太妃止贈二代，而況妃乎？」

translations.literal: At the Tiansheng suburban sacrifice the Grand Consort received only two generations — how much more so a consort?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Tiansheng suburban sacrifice the Grand Consort received only two generations of honors — how much less should a mere consort?"

sentences.zh: 英宗立，遇疾，慈聖光獻后同聽政。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended the throne he fell ill; Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian ruled jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong came to the throne he fell ill, and Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian ruled jointly with him.

sentences.zh: 光上疏曰：「昔章獻明肅有保佑先帝之功，特以親用外戚小人，負謗海內。

translations.literal: Guang submitted a memorial: "Formerly Empress Zhangxian Mingsu had the merit of protecting the late emperor, yet because she favored petty kinsmen and men she was reviled throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Guang memorialized: "Empress Zhangxian Mingsu once had the merit of safeguarding the late emperor, yet because she favored petty kinsmen and flatterers she was condemned throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 今攝政之際，大臣忠厚如王曾，清純如張知白，剛正如魯宗道，質直如薛奎者，當信用之；

translations.literal: Now in the period of regency, such ministers as the loyal Wang Zeng, the pure Zhang Zhibai, the upright Lu Zongdao, and the plainspoken Xue Kui ought to be trusted and employed;
translations.idiomatic: In the present regency, ministers as loyal as Wang Zeng, as upright as Zhang Zhibai, as firm as Lu Zongdao, and as direct as Xue Kui should be trusted and used;

sentences.zh: 猥鄙如馬季良，讒諂如羅崇勳者，當疏遠之，則天下服。」

translations.literal: men as base as Ma Jiliang and as slanderous as Luo Chongxun ought to be kept at a distance — then all under Heaven will be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: while men as vile as Ma Jiliang and as deceitful as Luo Chongxun should be kept far off — then the empire will be at ease."

sentences.zh: 帝疾愈，光料必有追隆本生事，即奏言：「漢宣帝為孝昭後，終不追尊衛太子、史皇孫；

translations.literal: When the Emperor recovered, Guang foresaw that there would surely be an effort to exalt his biological father; he immediately memorialized: "Emperor Xuan of Han succeeded Emperor Zhao and never posthumously honored Crown Prince Wei or the Emperor Grandson;
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor recovered, Guang foresaw a push to elevate his biological father and at once memorialized: "Emperor Xuan of Han succeeded Emperor Zhao yet never posthumously honored Crown Prince Wei or the Emperor Grandson;

sentences.zh: 光武上繼元帝，亦不追尊鉅鹿、南頓君，此萬世法也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu succeeded Emperor Yuan and likewise did not posthumously honor the lords of Julu and Nandun — this is the law for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu succeeded Emperor Yuan and likewise did not posthumously honor the lords of Julu and Nandun — that is the model for all ages."

sentences.zh: 後詔兩制集議濮王典禮，學士王珪等相視莫敢先，光獨奮筆書曰：「為人後者為之子，不得顧私親。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered the two academies to assemble and discuss rites for the Prince of Pu; the academicians Wang Gui and others looked at one another and none dared speak first; Guang alone took up his brush and wrote: "One who becomes another's heir is that person's son and may not look to his private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an edict ordered the Hanlin academicians to debate rites for the Prince of Pu, Wang Gui and the others exchanged glances and none dared speak first; Guang alone seized his brush and wrote: "He who becomes another's heir is that man's son and must not favor his private kin.

sentences.zh: 王宜凖封贈期親尊屬故事，稱為皇伯，高官大國，極其尊榮。」

translations.literal: By the precedents for enfeoffment and posthumous gifts to close agnates of the imperial house, he should be styled Imperial Uncle and given high office and a great fief — the utmost honor."
translations.idiomatic: Under the precedents for enfeoffment and posthumous honors for close imperial kin, he should be styled Imperial Uncle, with high rank and a great state — the fullest dignity allowed."

sentences.zh: 議成，珪即命吏以其手稿為按。

translations.literal: When the decision was settled, Gui immediately ordered clerks to take his manuscript as the basis.
translations.idiomatic: Once the decision was drafted, Gui at once ordered clerks to take Guang's manuscript as the official record.

sentences.zh: 既上與大臣意殊，御史六人爭之力，皆斥去。

translations.literal: After it was submitted it differed from the great ministers' view; six censorial investigators strove against it with all their force and were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Once submitted, the decision clashed with the chief ministers; six investigating censors fought it with all their strength and were all expelled.

sentences.zh: 光乞留之，不可，遂請與俱貶。

translations.literal: Guang begged that they be retained; it was not permitted; he then asked to be demoted together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Guang pleaded that they be kept; when refused, he asked to be demoted along with them.

sentences.zh: 初，西夏遣使致祭，延州指使高宜押伴，傲其使者，侮其國主，使者訴于朝。

translations.literal: Initially the Western Xia sent envoys to offer condolences; the Yanzhou commander Gao Yi escorted them as companion commissioner; he was arrogant toward the envoys and insulted their ruler; the envoys complained at court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Western Xia had sent envoys to offer condolences; the Yanzhou commander Gao Yi served as companion commissioner, behaved arrogantly toward the envoys, and insulted their ruler; the envoys lodged a complaint at court.

sentences.zh: 光與呂誨乞加宜罪，不從。

translations.literal: Guang and Lü Hui asked that Yi be punished more severely; the court did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and Lü Hui asked that Yi receive a heavier penalty; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，夏人犯邊，殺略吏士。

translations.literal: The next year the Western Xia raided the border and killed and plundered officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Western Xia invaded the frontier, killing and plundering officials and troops.

sentences.zh: 趙滋為雄州，專以猛悍治邊，光論其不可。

translations.literal: Zhao Zi was at Xiongzhou and governed the border solely by fierceness and harshness; Guang argued that this would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zi held Xiongzhou and governed the border solely through fierceness and harshness; Guang warned that this course was untenable.

sentences.zh: 至是，契丹之民捕魚界河，伐柳白溝之南，朝廷以知雄州李中祐為不材，將代之。

translations.literal: By then Khitan subjects were fishing in the border river and cutting willows south of the Bai Gou; the court considered Li Zhongyou, knower of Xiongzhou, incompetent and was about to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Khitan subjects were fishing in the border river and cutting willows south of the Bai Gou; the court judged Li Zhongyou, commissioner at Xiongzhou, incompetent and was about to replace him.

sentences.zh: 光謂：「國家當戎夷附順時，好與之計較末節，及其桀驁，又從而姑息之。

translations.literal: Guang said: "When the state faces compliant barbarians it haggles over petty details; when they grow arrogant it indulges them again.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "When barbarians are compliant we quarrel over trifles; when they grow defiant we indulge them again.

sentences.zh: 近者西禍生於高宜，北禍起于趙滋；

translations.literal: Recently the western disaster arose from Gao Yi, the northern from Zhao Zi;
translations.idiomatic: The recent western trouble sprang from Gao Yi, the northern from Zhao Zi;

sentences.zh: 時方賢此二人，故邊臣皆以生事為能，漸不可長。

translations.literal: yet at the time these two men were thought worthy, so frontier officers all took stirring up trouble as merit — this tendency must not be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: yet the court was praising both men, so border officers all treated provocation as achievement — a habit that must not be allowed to spread.

sentences.zh: 宜敕邊吏，疆場細故輒以矢刃相加者，罪之。」

translations.literal: I urge that frontier officers be instructed: whoever draws blades over trifling border matters shall be punished."
translations.idiomatic: I urge an order to frontier commanders: whoever resorts to arms over petty border incidents shall be punished."

sentences.zh: 仁宗遺賜直百餘萬，光率同列三上章，謂：「國有大憂，中外窘乏，不可專用乾興故事。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong bequeathed direct gifts of more than a million cash; Guang led his colleagues in three memorials saying: "The state has great mourning and court and country are straitened — we cannot follow the Qianxing precedent alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong left direct gifts of more than a million cash; Guang led his colleagues in three joint memorials: "The realm is in deep mourning and resources are strained at court and in the provinces — we cannot follow only the Qianxing precedent.

sentences.zh: 若遺賜不可辭，宜許侍從上進金錢佐山陵。」

translations.literal: If the bequest cannot be refused, the attendants should be permitted to offer money from their salaries to assist the imperial tomb."
translations.idiomatic: If the bequest cannot be declined, let attendants be allowed to contribute from their salaries toward the imperial tomb instead."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 光乃以所得珠為諫院公使錢，金以遺舅氏，義不藏於家。

translations.literal: Guang then took the pearls he received for the Remonstrance Bureau's public funds and gave the gold to his maternal uncle — on principle he would not keep them at home.
translations.idiomatic: Guang turned the pearls he received into public funds for the Remonstrance Bureau and gave the gold to his maternal uncle — he would not keep such gifts in his household.

sentences.zh: 后還政，有司立式，凡後有后取用，當覆奏乃供。

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned power; the relevant offices established a procedure: whenever the empress dowager later requested something, it should be supplied only after memorializing for approval.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager returned power, the relevant offices set a rule: whenever the empress dowager later made a request, supplies should be issued only after a memorial of approval.

sentences.zh: 光云：「當移所屬使立供已，乃具數白后，以防矯偽。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "The subordinate office should first prepare and supply, then report the quantities to the empress dowager — to guard against forgery."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "The responsible office should prepare and deliver first, then report the amounts to the empress dowager — that is how to guard against fraud."

sentences.zh: 曹佾無功除使相，兩府皆遷官。

translations.literal: Cao Yi was made commissioner and grand councilor without merit; both offices of the Secretariat were promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi was made military commissioner and grand councilor though he had no merit, and both Secretariat chancellors were promoted as well.

sentences.zh: 光言：「陛下欲以慰母心，而遷除無名，則宿衛將帥、內侍小臣，必有覬望。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "Your Majesty wished to comfort your mother's heart, but promotions without cause will make guards and generals, and petty inner attendants, all harbor expectations."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "Your Majesty meant to comfort your mother's heart, but rank granted without cause will teach palace guards, frontier generals, and petty attendants alike to expect the same."

sentences.zh: 已而遷都知任守忠等官，光復爭之，因論：「守忠大奸，陛下為皇子，非守忠意，沮壞大策，離間百端，賴先帝不聽；

translations.literal: Before long the chief inner attendant Ren Shouzhong and others were promoted; Guang again contended, and argued: "Shouzhong is a great villain — when Your Majesty was imperial son it was not Shouzhong's wish; he obstructed the great plan, sowed division on every side — only because the late emperor would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Soon the chief inner attendant Ren Shouzhong and others were promoted; Guang protested again, declaring: "Shouzhong is a great villain — when Your Majesty was named imperial son it was against his will; he thwarted the great design and sowed discord at every turn — only the late emperor's refusal to heed him saved the day;

sentences.zh: 及陛下嗣位，反覆交構，國之大賊。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty succeeded to the throne he repeatedly plotted and slandered — a great villain to the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty took the throne he plotted and slandered without cease — the empire's greatest villain.

sentences.zh: 乞斬于都市，以謝天下。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be executed in the marketplace to appease all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be put to death in the capital marketplace as satisfaction to the realm."

sentences.zh: 責守忠為節度副使，蘄州安置，天下快之。

translations.literal: Shouzhong was made military vice commissioner and resettled at Qizhou — all under Heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong was demoted to military vice commissioner and exiled to Qizhou for resettlement, to the relief of the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 詔刺陝西義勇二十萬，民情驚撓，而紀律疏略不可用。

translations.literal: An edict drafted two hundred thousand volunteers in Shaanxi; the people were alarmed and disturbed, yet discipline was lax and they could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called up two hundred thousand volunteers in Shaanxi; the populace was thrown into alarm, yet discipline was slack and the force proved unusable.

sentences.zh: 光抗言其非，持白韓琦。

translations.literal: Guang remonstrated that this was wrong and took a memorial to Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Guang protested vigorously and carried a memorial to Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「兵貴先聲，諒祚方桀驁，使驟聞益兵二十萬，豈不震懾？」

translations.literal: Qi said: "In war the first strike counts; Liangzuo is just now arrogant — if he suddenly hears we have added two hundred thousand troops, will he not be shaken?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "In warfare prestige strikes first; Liangzuo is at his most defiant — if he suddenly learns we have raised two hundred thousand men, will he not be terrified?"

sentences.zh: 光曰：「兵之貴先聲，為無其實也，獨可欺之於一日之間耳。

translations.literal: Guang said: "War values the first strike only when there is no substance behind it — you can deceive the enemy for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Guang replied: "The first strike avails only when there is no real force behind it — you may fool them for a day.

sentences.zh: 今吾雖益兵，實不可用，不過十日，彼將知其詳，尚何懼？」

translations.literal: Now though we add troops they are in fact unusable; in no more than ten days the enemy will know the truth — what is there left to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: We are adding men who cannot actually fight; within ten days they will know the full truth — what is left to fear?"

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「君但見慶曆間鄉兵刺為保捷，憂今復然，已降敕榜與民約，永不充軍戍邊矣。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "You only see that in the Qingli era village militia were drafted as permanent soldiers and fear the same now; we have already issued an edict promising the people they will never be conscripted for frontier garrison duty."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "You only recall how in the Qingli era local militia were turned into permanent troops and fear a repeat; we have already posted an edict pledging the people they will never be sent to garrison the frontier."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「朝廷嘗失信，民未敢以為然，雖光亦不能不疑也。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "The court has broken faith before; the people dare not believe it — even I cannot help doubting."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "The court has broken its word before; the people dare not trust this pledge — I myself cannot help doubting."

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「吾在此，君無憂。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "As long as I remain here, you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "While I hold office here, you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「公長在此地，可也；

translations.literal: Guang said: "If you remain in this post long, that may suffice;
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "You may remain in this post for now;

sentences.zh: 異日他人當位，因公見兵，用之運糧戍邊，反掌間事耳。」

translations.literal: but when another takes office, because of you he will see these troops and use them to transport grain and garrison the frontier — a matter accomplished in the turn of a hand."
translations.idiomatic: but when someone else succeeds you, seeing these troops he will press them into hauling grain and garrisoning the frontier — a thing done in the blink of an eye."

sentences.zh: 琦嘿然，而訖不為止。

translations.literal: Qi fell silent, yet in the end did not stop the policy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fell silent but never halted the policy.

sentences.zh: 不十年，皆如光慮。

translations.literal: Within ten years all came to pass as Guang had feared.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years everything unfolded as Guang had warned.

sentences.zh: 王廣淵除直集賢院，光論其奸邪不可近：「昔漢景帝重衛綰，周世宗薄張美。

translations.literal: Wang Guangyuan was appointed to direct access to the Hall of Assembled Worthies; Guang argued that his wickedness made him unapproachable: "Formerly Emperor Jing of Han valued Wei Wan; Emperor Shizong of Zhou despised Zhang Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangyuan was given direct access to the Hall of Assembled Worthies; Guang protested that his treachery made him unfit for proximity: "Emperor Jing of Han once prized Wei Wan; Emperor Shizong of Zhou looked down on Zhang Mei.

sentences.zh: 廣淵當仁宗之世，私自結于陛下，豈忠臣哉？

translations.literal: In Renzong's time Guangyuan privately attached himself to Your Majesty — is he a loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: During Renzong's reign Guangyuan cultivated Your Majesty in private — is that the conduct of a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 宜黜之以厲天下。」

translations.literal: He should be dismissed to admonish all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He should be removed to warn the whole empire."

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: Guang was promoted to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with direct access.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with direct access.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，擢為翰林學士，光力辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne Guang was elevated to Hanlin Academician; Guang strove to decline.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne Guang was elevated to Hanlin Academician, but he strove to decline.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古之君子，或學而不文，或文而不學，惟董仲舒、揚雄兼之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The gentlemen of antiquity either studied without literary skill or wrote without study — only Dong Zhongshu and Yang Xiong combined both.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Men of old either studied without literary grace or wrote without learning — only Dong Zhongshu and Yang Xiong united both.

sentences.zh: 卿有文學，何辭為？」

translations.literal: You have literary learning — why decline?"
translations.idiomatic: You possess both learning and letters — why refuse?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不能為四六。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant cannot write parallel prose in six parts."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I cannot compose the six-part parallel prose of court edicts."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如兩漢制詔可也；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The edicts of the two Han dynasties will suffice;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The plain edicts of the two Han dynasties will do;

sentences.zh: 且卿能進士取高第，而云不能四六，何邪？」

translations.literal: and you passed the jinshi in the top rank — yet say you cannot write parallel prose — how so?"
translations.idiomatic: besides, you placed in the top tier of the jinshi examinations — yet claim you cannot write parallel prose? How can that be?"

sentences.zh: 竟不獲辭。

translations.literal: In the end he could not decline.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王陶以論宰相不押班罷，光代之，光言：「陶由論宰相罷，則中丞不可復為。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Wang Tao was dismissed for criticizing the chief ministers' failure to attend court in rank order; Guang replaced him and said: "Tao was removed for criticizing the chief ministers — then the investigating censor cannot take up the post again.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wang Tao was dismissed for attacking the chief ministers' failure to attend court in rank order; when Guang was named to replace him he said: "Tao lost his post for criticizing the chief ministers — I cannot accept the censorate while that issue stands.

sentences.zh: 臣願俟既押班，然後就職。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks to wait until they again attend in rank order, then take office."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to wait until they resume attending in proper order, then take up the post."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 遂上疏論修心之要三：曰仁，曰明，曰武；

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial on the three essentials of cultivating the heart: benevolence, clarity, and martial resolve;
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized on the three essentials of cultivating the heart — benevolence, clarity, and martial resolve;

sentences.zh: 治國之要三：曰官人，曰信賞，曰必罰。

translations.literal: and the three essentials of governing the state: appointing men, rewarding faithfully, and punishing surely.
translations.idiomatic: and the three essentials of governing the state — appointing the right men, rewarding faithfully, and punishing without fail.

sentences.zh: 其說甚備。

translations.literal: His exposition was very complete.
translations.idiomatic: His exposition was thorough in every respect.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「臣獲事三朝，皆以此六言獻，平生力學所得，盡在是矣。」

translations.literal: He said: "Your servant has served three reigns and always offered these six words; what I have gained from a lifetime of study is all here."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "I have served three reigns and always offered these six principles; what a lifetime of study has taught me is contained in them alone."

sentences.zh: 御藥院內臣，國朝常用供奉官以下，至內殿崇班則出；

translations.literal: The Imperial Pharmacy used inner attendants; the dynasty customarily employed men below the rank of commissioner for attendance on the sovereign; once they reached inner palace attendant of the highest grade they were released;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Pharmacy was staffed by inner attendants; by dynastic custom posts below commissioner for attendance on the sovereign were used, and once a man reached inner palace attendant of the highest grade he left the post;

sentences.zh: 近歲暗理官資，非祖宗本意。

translations.literal: in recent years ranks were quietly purchased — not the intent of the founding ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: in recent years ranks had been quietly purchased — contrary to the founders' intent.

sentences.zh: 因論高居簡奸邪，乞加遠竄。

translations.literal: He also argued that Gao Jujian was wicked and begged that he be exiled far away.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced Gao Jujian as treacherous and begged that he be banished to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 章五上，帝為出居簡，盡罷寄資者。

translations.literal: After five memorials the Emperor removed Jujian and abolished all purchased ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After five memorials the Emperor removed Jujian and abolished all purchased ranks.

sentences.zh: 既而復留二人，光又力爭之。

translations.literal: Later two men were kept; Guang again strove against it.
translations.idiomatic: Later two men were retained; Guang protested again with all his force.

sentences.zh: 張方平參知政事，光論其不叶物望，帝不從。

translations.literal: Zhang Fangping was made participant in determining government affairs; Guang argued he did not meet public expectation; the Emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping was made participant in determining government affairs; Guang argued he lacked public confidence; the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 還光翰林兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Guang was returned to Hanlin with concurrent post as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was returned to the Hanlin Academy with a concurrent post as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 光常患歷代史繁，人主不能遍鑒，遂為《通志》八卷以獻。

translations.literal: Guang often grieved that historical records of successive dynasties were too vast for a ruler to survey entirely; he therefore compiled the Comprehensive Mirror in eight juan and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had long lamented that the histories of successive dynasties were too vast for any ruler to survey; he therefore compiled the Comprehensive Mirror in eight juan and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 英宗悅之，命置局秘閣，續其書。

translations.literal: Yingzong was pleased and ordered a bureau set up in the Secret Repository to continue the work.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong was delighted and ordered a bureau established in the Secret Repository to continue the work.

sentences.zh: 至是，神宗名之曰《資治通鑒》，自製《序》授之，俾日進讀。

translations.literal: By then Shenzong named it Mirror for Aid in Government and himself composed a Preface to confer on Guang, ordering him to read from it daily.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shenzong named it the Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, composed a Preface himself, and commanded Guang to read from it daily at court.

sentences.zh: 詔錄潁邸直省官四人為閤門祗候，光曰：「國初草創，天步尚艱，故御極之初，必以左右舊人為腹心耳目，謂之隨龍，非平日法也。

translations.literal: An edict selected four direct clerks of the Prince of Ying's household as palace gate attendants; Guang said: "In the founding of the dynasty the imperial steps were still perilous, so at the beginning of rule one necessarily relied on old companions as heart, eyes, and ears — called "followers of the dragon" — not the regular law of peaceful times.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named four direct clerks from the Prince of Ying's household as palace gate attendants; Guang objected: "At the dynasty's founding the throne was still insecure, so a new ruler necessarily relied on old companions as eyes and ears — the so-called followers of the dragon — not the regular practice of settled times.

sentences.zh: 閤門祗候在文臣為館職，豈可使廝役為之。」

translations.literal: Palace gate attendants among civil officials are academy posts — how can menials be appointed to them?"
translations.idiomatic: Among civil officials palace gate attendants are academy posts — how can lackeys fill them?"

sentences.zh: 西戎部將嵬名山欲以橫山之眾，取諒祚以降，詔邊臣招納其眾。

translations.literal: A Western Xia frontier officer named Wei Mingshan wished to use the forces of Hengshan to seize Liangzuo and surrender; an edict ordered frontier officials to recruit his followers.
translations.idiomatic: A Western Xia frontier officer named Wei Mingshan wished to use the Hengshan tribes to seize Liangzuo and surrender; the court ordered frontier officials to recruit his followers.

sentences.zh: 光上疏極論，以為：「名山之眾，未必能制諒祚。

translations.literal: Guang submitted a memorial arguing at length that "Mingshan's followers cannot necessarily control Liangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Guang memorialized at length: "Mingshan's followers may not be able to control Liangzuo at all.

sentences.zh: 幸而勝之，滅一諒祚，生一諒祚，何利之有；

translations.literal: If by chance they succeed, one Liangzuo is destroyed and one Liangzuo is born — what profit is there?
translations.idiomatic: If they win, we destroy one Liangzuo only to create another — what gain is that?

sentences.zh: 若其不勝，必引眾歸我，不知何以待之。

translations.literal: If they fail, they will surely lead their followers to us — I do not know how we are to treat them.
translations.idiomatic: If they lose, they will surely bring their followers to us — and I do not know how we are to receive them.

sentences.zh: 臣恐朝廷不獨失信諒祚，又將失信於名山矣。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the court will not only break faith with Liangzuo but also break faith with Mingshan.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the court will break faith not only with Liangzuo but with Mingshan as well.

sentences.zh: 若名山餘眾尚多，還北不可，入南不受，窮無所歸，必將突據邊城以救其命。

translations.literal: If Mingshan's remaining followers are still numerous, they cannot return north and the south will not accept them — with nowhere to go they will surely raid the border towns to save their lives.
translations.idiomatic: If many of Mingshan's followers remain, they cannot go back north and the south will not take them in; desperate and with nowhere to turn, they will surely strike border towns to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 陛下不見侯景之事乎？」

translations.literal: Has Your Majesty not seen what became of Hou Jing?"
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty forgotten what became of Hou Jing?"

sentences.zh: 上不聽，遣將种諤發兵迎之，取綏州，費六十萬，西方用兵，蓋自此始矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen; he sent the general Chong E to lead troops to receive them and seize Suizhou at a cost of six hundred thousand — frontier warfare in the west began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not listen; he sent the general Chong E to lead troops to receive them and seized Suizhou at a cost of six hundred thousand — western campaigns began from this.

sentences.zh: 百官上尊號，光當答詔，言：「先帝親郊，不受尊號。

translations.literal: All officials offered honorific titles; Guang was to draft the reply and said: "The late emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice and refused honorific titles.
translations.idiomatic: When all officials offered honorific titles, Guang was to draft the reply and wrote: "The late emperor performed the suburban sacrifice in person and refused such titles.

sentences.zh: 末年有獻議者，謂國家與契丹往來通信，彼有尊號我獨無，於是復以非時奉冊。

translations.literal: In his last years some proposed that since in dealings with the Khitan we exchanged letters and they had honorific titles while we had none, the titles were again offered out of season.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years some argued that because we exchanged letters with the Khitan and they bore honorific titles while we did not, the titles were again offered at an improper time.

sentences.zh: 昔匈奴冒頓自稱『天地所生日月所置匈奴大單于』，不聞漢文帝復為大名以加之也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Xiongnu chanyu Maodun styled himself "Great Chanyu Established by Heaven and Earth, by the Sun and Moon" — one never heard that Emperor Wen of Han fashioned a great title to match it.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Xiongnu chanyu Maodun called himself the Great Chanyu Established by Heaven and Earth and the Sun and Moon — yet Emperor Wen of Han never fashioned a grand title to match his.

sentences.zh: 願追述先帝本意，不受此名。」

translations.literal: I pray we follow the late emperor's original intent and refuse this name."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that we follow the late emperor's original intent and refuse these titles."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，手詔獎光，使善為答辭，以示中外。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, personally drafted an edict praising Guang, and had him compose a fine reply to show court and country.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased, personally drafted an edict praising Guang, and had him compose an elegant reply for all court and country to see.

sentences.zh: 執政以河朔旱傷，國用不足，乞南郊勿賜金帛。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, citing drought damage in Hebei and insufficient state revenue, asked that gold and silk not be distributed at the southern suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, citing drought damage in Hebei and short revenue, asked that gold and silk not be distributed at the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詔學士議，光與王珪、王安石同見，光曰：「救災節用，宜自貴近始，可聽也。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered the academicians to discuss it; Guang met with Wang Gui and Wang Anshi and said: "Relief and frugality should begin with those nearest the throne — this may be allowed."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the academicians to discuss it; Guang met with Wang Gui and Wang Anshi and said: "Disaster relief and economy should begin with those nearest the throne — that may be allowed."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「常袞辭堂饌，時以為袞自知不能，當辭位不當辭祿。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Chang Gun once declined his hall meal — the age thought Gun knew his incapacity and ought to have resigned his post rather than his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said: "Chang Gun once refused his stipend at court — men of the time thought he knew his limits and should have resigned his office, not merely his salary.

sentences.zh: 且國用不足，非當世急務，所以不足者，以未得善理財者故也。」

translations.literal: Moreover insufficient state revenue is not the urgent task of the age; the reason for insufficiency is simply that we have not yet found a man skilled at managing finances."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, short revenue is not the age's true emergency; we lack only a man who knows how to manage the treasury well."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「善理財者，不過頭會箕斂爾。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "A man skilled at managing finances is nothing but one who squeezes the people with comb and dustpan."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "A skilled financier is nothing but one who wrings the people dry with comb and dustpan."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「不然，善理財者，不加賦而國用足。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Not so — a skilled financier adds no new levies yet fills the state coffers."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi replied: "Not so — a skilled financier fills the treasury without raising new taxes."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「天下安有此理？

translations.literal: Guang said: "Is there such a principle under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "Can such a thing exist under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 天地所生財貨百物，不在民，則在官，彼設法奪民，其害乃甚於加賦。

translations.literal: The wealth and goods produced by heaven and earth lie either with the people or with the officials; if you devise methods to seize from the people, the harm is worse than adding levies.
translations.idiomatic: All wealth produced by heaven and earth lies either with the people or with the state; if you devise schemes to seize it from the people, the harm is worse than new taxes.

sentences.zh: 此蓋桑羊欺武帝之言，太史公書之以見其不明耳。」

translations.literal: This is the deception Sang Hongyang practiced on Emperor Wu — the Grand Historian recorded it to show his lack of discernment."
translations.idiomatic: That is the deception Sang Hongyang practiced on Emperor Wu — the Grand Historian recorded it to expose his folly."

sentences.zh: 爭議不已。

translations.literal: The dispute continued without end.
translations.idiomatic: The argument would not end.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕意與光同，然姑以不允答之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "My mind agrees with Guang, yet for now I shall answer with refusal."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "My own view agrees with Guang, yet for the moment I shall answer with a refusal."

sentences.zh: 會安石草詔，引常袞事責兩府，兩府不敢復辭。

translations.literal: When Anshi drafted the edict he cited Chang Gun's case to rebuke the two offices; the two offices dared not argue further.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi drafted the reply he cited Chang Gun to rebuke the Secretariat chancellors, who dared not protest further.

sentences.zh: 安石得政，行新法，光逆疏其利害。

translations.literal: When Anshi took power he enacted the New Policies; Guang repeatedly memorialized against their harms.
translations.idiomatic: Once Anshi took power he enacted the New Policies; Guang repeatedly memorialized against their harm.

sentences.zh: 邇英進讀，至曹參代蕭何事，帝曰：「漢常守蕭何之法不變，可乎？」

translations.literal: During lecture at the Hall for Cultivating Virtue they came to Cao Shen succeeding Xiao He; the Emperor said: "The Han often kept Xiao He's laws unchanged — may one do so?"
translations.idiomatic: During lecture at the Hall for Cultivating Virtue they reached Cao Shen succeeding Xiao He; the Emperor asked: "The Han often kept Xiao He's laws unchanged — is that permissible?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「寧獨漢也，使三代之君常守禹、湯、文、武之法，雖至今存可也。

translations.literal: He replied: "It is not only the Han — if rulers of the Three Dynasties had constantly kept the laws of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, they might exist even to the present.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Not only the Han — if the rulers of the Three Dynasties had steadfastly kept the laws of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, those dynasties might stand even today.

sentences.zh: 漢武取高帝約束紛更，盜賊半天下；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han took Gaodi's constraints and changed them in confusion — bandits filled half the empire;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han abandoned Gaozu's constraints and changed them recklessly — rebels filled half the empire;

sentences.zh: 元帝改孝宣之政，漢業遂衰。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan altered Emperor Xuan's policies and the Han enterprise declined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan altered Xuan's policies and the Han cause declined.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，祖宗之法不可變也。」

translations.literal: From this it follows that the laws of the founding ancestors cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the laws of the founding ancestors must not be changed."

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿言：「先王之法，有一年一變者，『正月始和，布法象魏』是也；

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing said: "The laws of the former kings had some that changed every year — "In the first month harmony begins, proclaim the law at the gate" is such;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing said: "The former kings' laws included some that changed yearly — the line "In the first month harmony begins, proclaim the law at the gate" is one;

sentences.zh: 有五年一變者，巡守考制度是也；

translations.literal: some that changed every five years — the imperial tour to inspect and examine institutions is such;
translations.idiomatic: some that changed every five years — the imperial tour to inspect institutions is one;

sentences.zh: 有三十年一變者，『刑罰世輕世重』是也。

translations.literal: some that changed every thirty years — "Punishments light in one age, heavy in another" is such.
translations.idiomatic: some that changed every thirty years — "Punishments light in one age, heavy in another" is one.

sentences.zh: 光言非是，其意以風朝廷耳。」

translations.literal: Guang's words are wrong; his intent is to sway the court by rumor."
translations.idiomatic: Guang is mistaken; he only means to sway the court with clever talk."

sentences.zh: 帝問光，光曰：「『布法象魏』，布舊法也。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Guang; Guang said: ""Proclaim the law at the gate" means proclaim the old law.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor turned to Guang; he said: ""Proclaim the law at the gate" means proclaim the existing law.

sentences.zh: 諸侯變禮易樂者，王巡守則誅之，不自變也。

translations.literal: If a feudal lord altered ritual or music, when the king made his tour he executed him — the king did not change them himself.
translations.idiomatic: If a feudal lord altered ritual or music, the king on his tour punished him — the king did not change them himself.

sentences.zh: 刑新國用輕典，亂國用重典，是為『世輕世重』，非變也。

translations.literal: A new state uses light punishments, a chaotic state heavy ones — that is "light in one age, heavy in another" — not change.
translations.idiomatic: A newly founded state uses light punishments, a chaotic state heavy ones — that is "light in one age, heavy in another," not alteration.

sentences.zh: 且治天下譬如居室，敝則修之，非大壞不更造也。

translations.literal: Moreover governing the empire is like dwelling in a house — when it is worn one repairs it; one does not rebuild unless it is utterly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the empire is like keeping a house — when it wears one repairs it; one does not tear it down and rebuild unless it is utterly ruined.

sentences.zh: 公卿侍從皆在此，願陛下問之。

translations.literal: The chief ministers and attendants are all here — I pray Your Majesty ask them.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers and attendants are all present — I beg Your Majesty to ask them.

sentences.zh: 三司使掌天下財，不才而黜可也，不可使執政侵其事。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Three Departments manages the empire's wealth — if he is incompetent, dismiss him; but do not let the chief ministers encroach on his office.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Three Departments manages the realm's finances — if he is unfit, remove him; but do not let the chief ministers invade his charge.

sentences.zh: 今為制置三司條例司，何也？

translations.literal: Now you have created a Bureau for the Fiscal Regulations of the Three Departments — why?
translations.idiomatic: Now you have created a Bureau for the Fiscal Regulations of the Three Departments — for what reason?

sentences.zh: 宰相以道佐人主，安用例？

translations.literal: The chief minister assists the ruler by the Way — what need has he of precedents?
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister assists the ruler by moral principle — what need has he of precedent cases?

sentences.zh: 苟用例，則胥吏矣。

translations.literal: If he relies on precedents, he becomes a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: If he relies on precedents, he becomes a mere clerk.

sentences.zh: 今為看詳中書條例司，何也？」

translations.literal: Now you have created a Bureau to Review Regulations of the Secretariat — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you have created a Bureau to Review Regulations of the Secretariat — why?"

sentences.zh: 惠卿不能對，則以他語詆光。

translations.literal: Huiqing could not answer and turned to other words to slander Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing could not reply and turned to other topics to attack Guang.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「相與論是非耳，何至是。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "We are debating right and wrong — why go so far."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "We are debating right and wrong — why descend to this?"

sentences.zh: 光曰：「平民舉錢出息，尚能蠶食下戶，況縣官督責之威乎！」

translations.literal: Guang said: "When commoners lend money for interest they can still devour the households below them — how much more when the magistracy enforces collection with its authority!"
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "When commoners lend at interest they can still devour poorer households — how much worse when the magistracy enforces collection with state power!"

sentences.zh: 惠卿曰：「青苗法，願取則與之，不願不強也。」

translations.literal: Huiqing said: "Under the Green Sprouts law, those who wish to borrow receive it; those who do not wish it are not compelled."
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing said: "Under the Green Sprouts law, those who wish to borrow may; those who do not are not forced."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「愚民知取債之利，不知還債之害，非獨縣官不強，富民亦不強也。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Foolish people know the profit of taking a loan but not the harm of repaying it — it is not only the magistracy that does not compel; wealthy households do not compel either.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "Simple folk know the benefit of borrowing but not the pain of repayment — it is not only officials who do not force them; wealthy lenders do not force them either.

sentences.zh: 昔太宗平河東，立糴法，時米斗十錢，民樂與官為市。

translations.literal: Formerly when Taizong pacified Hedong he established the grain-purchase law; at the time grain was ten cash per dou and the people were glad to trade with the government.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong pacified Hedong he established the grain-purchase law; grain was then ten cash per dou and the people gladly sold to the government.

sentences.zh: 其後物貴而和糴不解，遂為河東世世患。

translations.literal: Later when goods grew dear the compulsory purchase was not lifted — it became Hedong's affliction for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when prices rose, the compulsory purchase was never lifted — it became a curse on Hedong for generations.

sentences.zh: 臣恐異日之青苗，亦猶是也。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that in days to come Green Sprouts will be the same."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in time Green Sprouts will prove the same."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「坐倉糴米何如？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What of storing grain in government granaries?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "What of storing grain in government granaries?"

sentences.zh: 坐者皆起，光曰：「不便。」

translations.literal: All those seated rose; Guang said: "It is not expedient."
translations.idiomatic: All those present rose; Guang said: "That is inexpedient."

sentences.zh: 惠卿曰：「糴米百萬斛，則省東南之漕，以其錢供京師。」

translations.literal: Huiqing said: "If we purchase a million hu of grain, we can dispense with transport tribute from the southeast and use that money to supply the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing said: "Buy a million hu of grain and we can skip the southeast transport tribute, using the saved funds for the capital instead."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「東南錢荒而粒米狼戾，今不糴米而漕錢，棄其有餘，取其所無，農末皆病矣！」

translations.literal: Guang said: "In the southeast there is a shortage of money while grain lies abundant; now, instead of purchasing grain, you would transport money — discarding what they have in surplus and taking what they lack — both farming and commerce will be harmed!"
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "The southeast lacks coin while grain rots in abundance. To transport money instead of buying grain is to abandon what they have in surplus and seize what they lack — farmers and merchants alike will suffer!"

sentences.zh: 侍講吳申起曰：「光言，至論也。」

translations.literal: The Lecturer-in-Waiting Wu Shen rose and said: "Guang's words are the ultimate argument."
translations.idiomatic: The Lecturer-in-Waiting Wu Shen rose and said: "Guang has stated the final truth."

sentences.zh: 它日留對，帝曰：「今天下洶洶者，孫叔敖所謂『國之有是，眾之所惡』也。」

translations.literal: Another day, kept for a private audience, the Emperor said: "The unrest throughout the realm today is what Sun Shu'ao called 'what the state has is what the multitude detests.'"
translations.idiomatic: On another day, kept back for a private audience, the Emperor said: "The turmoil across the realm is what Sun Shu'ao meant when he said the state possesses what the people hate."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「然。

translations.literal: Guang said: "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "That is so.

sentences.zh: 陛下當論其是非。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to judge right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should judge what is right and what is wrong.

sentences.zh: 今條例司所為，獨安石、韓絳、惠卿以為是耳，陛下豈能獨與此三人共為天下邪？」

translations.literal: What the Regulations Office has done — only Anshi, Han Jiang, and Huiqing deem it right; can Your Majesty govern the realm together with only these three men?"
translations.idiomatic: Only Anshi, Han Jiang, and Huiqing approve what the Regulations Office has done — can Your Majesty run the empire with just these three?"

sentences.zh: 帝欲用光，訪之安石。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to employ Guang and consulted Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted to appoint Guang and asked Anshi's opinion.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「光外託劘上之名，內懷附下之實。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Guang outwardly claims the name of vigorously serving the sovereign, but inwardly harbors the reality of winning favor below.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said: "Guang outwardly poses as a fierce loyalist, but inwardly courts popularity among the people.

sentences.zh: 所言盡害政之事，所與盡害政之人，而欲置之左右，使與國論，此消長之大機也。

translations.literal: Everything he speaks of are matters harmful to governance; everyone he associates with are people harmful to governance — yet you would place him at your side to discuss state affairs; this is the great pivot of waxing and waning.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he says undermines good government; everyone he keeps company with undermines good government. To put him at your side and let him debate state policy — that is the great turning point between advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 光才豈能害政，但在高位，則異論之人倚以為重。

translations.literal: Guang's talent could not harm governance in itself, but if placed in high office, those of divergent opinion would lean on him for weight.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's abilities alone would not ruin policy, but in high office he would give dissenters something to rally around.

sentences.zh: 韓信立漢赤幟，趙卒氣奪，今用光，是與異論者立赤幟也。」

translations.literal: When Han Xin raised the red banner of Han, the soldiers of Zhao lost their spirit; to employ Guang now is to raise a red banner for those of divergent opinion."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xin raised the red banner of Han, the Zhao troops lost heart. Appoint Guang now and you raise a red banner for the opposition."

sentences.zh: 安石以韓琦上疏，臥家求退。

translations.literal: Anshi, because Han Qi had submitted a memorial, remained at home requesting to resign.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Qi submitted a memorial, Anshi stayed home and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝乃拜光樞密副使，光辭之曰：「陛下所以用臣，蓋察其狂直，庶有補於國家。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon appointed Guang Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Guang declined, saying: "Your Majesty's reason for employing your servant is presumably that you perceive his forthright bluntness and hope it may benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then appointed Guang Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Guang declined: "Your Majesty means to use me, I suppose, because you see my blunt honesty and hope it will serve the state.

sentences.zh: 若徒以祿位榮之，而不取其言，是以天官私非其人也。

translations.literal: If you merely honor him with salary and rank but do not heed his words, you would be using the offices of Heaven for private ends — not for the right man.
translations.idiomatic: If you honor me with salary and rank but ignore what I say, you are filling a heavenly office with the wrong man for private ends.

sentences.zh: 臣徒以祿位自榮，而不能救生民之患，是盜竊名器以私其身也。

translations.literal: Your servant, merely taking salary and rank for his own glory without saving the people's distress, would be stealing the tokens of office for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: For me to take salary and rank for my own glory while failing to relieve the people's suffering would be to steal the insignia of office for private profit.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能罷制置條例司，追還提舉官，不行青苗、助役等法，雖不用臣，臣受賜多矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly abolish the Regulations Commission, recall the supervising commissioners, and cease the Green Sprouts, Labor Exemption, and other laws — even if you do not employ your servant, he would have received great favor.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will abolish the Regulations Commission, recall its commissioners, and stop the Green Sprouts, Labor Exemption, and the rest — even if you never appoint me, I will already have received a great boon.

sentences.zh: 今言青苗之害者，不過謂使者騷動州縣，為今日之患耳。

translations.literal: Those who speak of Green Sprouts' harm speak only of envoys disturbing prefectures and counties — a present-day affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Those who complain of Green Sprouts speak only of commissioners harassing the prefectures and counties — a problem for today.

sentences.zh: 而臣之所憂，乃在十年之外，非今日也。

translations.literal: But what your servant fears lies ten years hence, not today.
translations.idiomatic: What I fear lies ten years ahead, not in the present.

sentences.zh: 夫民之貧富，由勤惰不同，惰者常乏，故必資於人。

translations.literal: The wealth and poverty of the people arise from differences in diligence and sloth; the slothful are always in want and must rely on others.
translations.idiomatic: Some people are rich and some poor because some are diligent and some are idle; the idle are always short and must borrow from others.

sentences.zh: 今出錢貸民而斂其息，富者不願取，使者以多散為功，一切抑配。

translations.literal: Now money is lent to the people and interest collected; the wealthy do not wish to borrow, but envoys take wide distribution as their achievement and forcibly assign loans to all.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state lends money and collects interest. The wealthy do not want the loans, but commissioners treat wide distribution as merit and forcibly assign debt to everyone.

sentences.zh: 恐其逋負，必令貧富相保，貧者無可償，則散而之四方；

translations.literal: Fearing default, they require rich and poor to mutual guarantee one another; when the poor have nothing to repay, they scatter in all directions;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing default, they make rich and poor guarantee one another. When the poor cannot repay, they flee in every direction;

sentences.zh: 富者不能去，必責使代償數家之負。

translations.literal: The rich who cannot leave are compelled to repay the debts of several households in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are rich and cannot flee are forced to cover the debts of several households.

sentences.zh: 春算秋計，輾轉日滋，貧者既盡，富者亦貧。

translations.literal: Spring reckoning and autumn accounting grow by compounding day by day; when the poor are exhausted, the rich too become poor.
translations.idiomatic: Debts reckoned in spring and settled in autumn compound day by day. When the poor are ruined, the rich become poor as well.

sentences.zh: 十年之外，百姓無復存者矣。

translations.literal: Beyond ten years, none among the common people will survive.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years, no common people will be left.

sentences.zh: 又盡散常平錢穀，專行青苗，它日若思復之，將何所取？

translations.literal: Moreover the Ever-Normal granary funds and grain are entirely dispersed for Green Sprouts alone; if one day you wish to restore them, whence will you draw?
translations.idiomatic: And the Ever-Normal reserves of money and grain are spent entirely on Green Sprouts. If you later wish to restore them, where will the funds come from?

sentences.zh: 富室既盡，常平已廢，加之以師旅，因之以饑饉，民之羸者必委死溝壑，壯者必聚而為盜賊，此事之必至者也。」

translations.literal: When wealthy households are exhausted and the Ever-Normal system abolished, add military campaigns and famine — the frail will surely die in ditches and gullies, the strong will surely gather and become bandits; this must inevitably come to pass."
translations.idiomatic: Once the wealthy are ruined and the Ever-Normal system gone, add war and famine on top — the weak will die in ditches, the strong will band together as robbers. This must come to pass."

sentences.zh: 抗章至七八，帝使謂曰：「樞密，兵事也，官各有職，不當以他事為辭。」

translations.literal: He submitted remonstrances seven or eight times; the Emperor sent word saying: "The Bureau of Military Affairs is for military affairs; each office has its duties — you ought not decline on other grounds."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials seven or eight times. The Emperor sent word: "Military Affairs handles military matters. Each office has its charge — you should not refuse the post on other grounds."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣未受命，則猶侍從也，于事無不可言者。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant has not yet received the appointment — he is still an attendant — and there is nothing he may not speak of regarding affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I have not yet taken the appointment — I am still an attendant — and there is nothing I may not speak about."

sentences.zh: 安石起視事，光乃得請，遂求去。

translations.literal: Anshi resumed his duties; Guang then obtained his request and sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi returned to office; Guang got his way and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 以端明殿學士知永興軍。

translations.literal: He was made Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness and assigned to govern Yongxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness and put in charge of Yongxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使下令分義勇戍邊，選諸軍驍勇士，募市井惡少年為奇兵；
