translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner ordered the militia divided to garrison the frontier, selected fierce brave soldiers from the various armies, and recruited wicked youths from the marketplaces as special troops;
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commissioner ordered the militia split to garrison the border, picked the fiercest soldiers from the regular armies, and recruited rowdy youths from the markets as strike forces;

sentences.zh: 調民造乾糒，悉修城池樓櫓，關輔騷然。

translations.literal: Drafted the people to make dried rations, and fully repaired city walls and watchtowers — the capital region was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He conscripted civilians to make dried provisions and fully rebuilt walls and towers — the capital region was thrown into uproar.

sentences.zh: 光極言：「公私困敝，不可舉事，而京兆一路皆內郡，繕治非急。

translations.literal: Guang strongly argued: "Public and private resources are exhausted — military action is impossible; moreover the entire Jingzhao route consists of inner prefectures — fortification is not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Guang protested vigorously: "Public and private resources are exhausted — we cannot launch campaigns. The whole Jingzhao route lies in the interior; fortifications are not urgent.

sentences.zh: 宣撫之令，皆未敢從，若乏軍興，臣當任其責。」

translations.literal: I have not dared comply with any of the Pacification Commissioner's orders; if there is a shortfall for military expenditure, your servant will bear the responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: I have not dared obey any of the Pacification Commissioner's orders. If military funds fall short, I will take the blame."

sentences.zh: 於是一路獨得免。

translations.literal: Thereupon this circuit alone was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, this circuit alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 徙知許州，趣入覲，不赴；

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Xuzhou; ordered to come for an audience, he did not go;
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xuzhou. Summoned to court, he did not go;

sentences.zh: 請判西京御史臺歸洛，自是絕口不論事。

translations.literal: Requested appointment as judge of the Western Capital Censorate and returned to Luoyang — from then on he ceased entirely to speak of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to serve as judge of the Western Capital Censorate and returned to Luoyang. From then on he kept silent on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 而求言詔下，光讀之感泣，欲嘿不忍，乃復陳六事，又移書責宰相吳充，事見《充傳》。

translations.literal: But when an edict soliciting advice was issued, Guang read it and wept; wanting to remain silent he could not bear to, and so again laid out six matters, also sending a letter rebuking the Chief Councillor Wu Chong — the account appears in Wu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict soliciting advice was issued, Guang read it and wept. He wanted to stay silent but could not, and so again set forth six points and wrote a letter rebuking Chief Councillor Wu Chong — the details appear in Wu's biography.

sentences.zh: 蔡天申為察訪，妄作威福，河南尹、轉運使敬事之如上官；

translations.literal: Cai Tianshen served as an investigatory commissioner and arrogated power; the Intendant of Henan and the Transport Commissioner treated him reverentially as a superior officer;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Tianshen served as an investigatory commissioner and abused his authority. The Intendant of Henan and the Transport Commissioner treated him like a superior;

sentences.zh: 嘗朝謁應天院神御殿，府獨為設一班，示不敢與抗。

translations.literal: Once when he attended court to pay homage at the Imperial Spirit Hall of Yingtian Court, the prefecture alone arranged a separate rank for him, showing they dared not contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he attended court at the Imperial Spirit Hall in Yingtian Court, the prefecture alone set aside a separate place in the ranks for him, showing they dared not stand against him.

sentences.zh: 光顧謂臺吏曰：「引蔡寺丞歸本班。」

translations.literal: Guang turned and said to the Censorate clerks: "Lead Vice-Director Cai back to his proper rank."
translations.idiomatic: Guang turned to the Censorate clerks and said: "Bring Vice-Director Cai back to his proper place in the ranks."

sentences.zh: 吏即引天申立監竹木務官富贊善之下。

translations.literal: The clerks at once led Tianshen to stand below Fu Zanshan, supervisor of the bamboo and timber office.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks immediately placed Tianshen below Fu Zanshan, supervisor of the bamboo and timber office.

sentences.zh: 天申窘沮，即日行。

translations.literal: Tianshen, abashed and crestfallen, departed that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Tianshen left that very day.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，忽得語澀疾，疑且死，豫作遺表置臥內，即有緩急，當以畀所善者上之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he suddenly developed a speech impediment; suspecting he was near death, he prepared a final memorial in advance and kept it within his bedchamber — if there were sudden crisis it was to be given to a trusted person to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he suddenly developed a speech disorder. Fearing he might die, he prepared a final memorial in advance and kept it by his bed — if crisis came, a trusted friend was to submit it.

sentences.zh: 官制行，帝指御史大夫曰：「非司馬光不可。」

translations.literal: When the new government structure took effect, the Emperor pointed to the Grand Censor and said: "No one but Sima Guang will do."
translations.idiomatic: When the new official hierarchy took effect, the Emperor pointed to the post of Grand Censor and said: "Only Sima Guang will do."

sentences.zh: 又將以為東宮師傅。

translations.literal: He was also about to be made tutor to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also intended to make him tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 蔡確曰：「國是方定，願少遲之。」

translations.literal: Cai Que said: "The settled policy of the state has only just been fixed — I hope it may be delayed a little."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que said: "The national policy has only just been settled — I hope this can wait a little longer."

sentences.zh: 《資治通鑒》未就，帝尤重之，以為賢于荀悅《漢紀》，數促使終篇，賜以潁邸舊書二千四百卷。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government was not yet complete; the Emperor especially prized it, deeming it superior to Xun Yue's Annals of Han, repeatedly urging him to finish it, and bestowing on him 2,400 volumes of old books from the Ying palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government was still unfinished. The Emperor valued it above all, judging it superior to Xun Yue's Annals of Han. He repeatedly pressed Guang to finish it and gave him 2,400 volumes of old books from the Ying palace.

sentences.zh: 及書成，加資政殿學士。

translations.literal: When the work was complete, he was given the additional title Academician of the Hall of Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was finished, he received the additional title Academician of the Hall of Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡居洛陽十五年，天下以為真宰相，田夫野老皆號為「司馬相公」，婦人孺子亦知其為君實也。

translations.literal: In all he dwelt in Luoyang fifteen years; the realm regarded him as the true prime minister — farmers and rustics all called him "Prime Minister Sima," and even women and children knew he was Junshi.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Luoyang for fifteen years in all. The empire treated him as the real prime minister — farmers and villagers all called him "Prime Minister Sima," and even women and children knew him as Junshi.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，赴闕臨，衛士望見，皆以手加額曰：「此司馬相公也。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, he went to the capital for the mourning; the guards saw him and all placed their hands to their foreheads, saying: "This is Prime Minister Sima."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor died, Guang went to the capital for the mourning. The guards saw him and touched their foreheads in salute: "It is Prime Minister Sima."

sentences.zh: 所至，民遮道聚觀，馬至不得行，曰：「公無歸洛，留相天子，活百姓。」

translations.literal: Wherever he went, the people blocked the road to gather and watch — his horse could not advance — crying: "Sir, do not return to Luoyang — stay to assist the Son of Heaven and save the people."
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, crowds blocked the road until his horse could not pass, crying: "Sir, do not go back to Luoyang — stay at court to serve the Son of Heaven and save the people."

sentences.zh: 哲宗幼沖，太皇太后臨政，遣使問所當先，光謂：「開言路。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong was young; the Empress Dowager held court; she sent envoys asking what should come first — Guang said: "Open the avenue of speech."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong was still a child. The Empress Dowager ruled in his stead and sent envoys to ask what should be done first. Guang said: "Open the channels of remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 詔榜朝堂。

translations.literal: An edict was posted in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was posted in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 而大臣有不悅者，設六語云：「若陰有所懷，犯非其分；

translations.literal: But some ministers who were displeased devised six phrases, saying: "If one secretly harbors ulterior motives and oversteps one's proper role;
translations.idiomatic: But displeased ministers devised six forbidden phrases: "If one secretly harbors hidden designs and oversteps one's proper role;

sentences.zh: 或扇搖機事之重；

translations.literal: or agitates weighty affairs of state;
translations.idiomatic: or stirs up weighty matters of state;

sentences.zh: 或迎合已行之令；

translations.literal: or flatters policies already implemented;
translations.idiomatic: or panders to policies already in force;

sentences.zh: 上以徼幸希進，下以眩惑流俗。

translations.literal: seeking advancement through opportunism above, or beguiling the common crowd below.
translations.idiomatic: seeking promotion through flattery above, or misleading the common people below.

sentences.zh: 若此者，罰無赦。」

translations.literal: Whoever does such things shall be punished without mercy."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever does these things shall be punished without pardon."

sentences.zh: 後復命示光，光曰：「此非求諫，乃拒諫也。

translations.literal: Later the command was shown to Guang again; Guang said: "This is not seeking remonstrance — it is refusing remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The draft was shown to Guang again. Guang said: "This is not inviting criticism — it is blocking criticism.

sentences.zh: 人臣惟不言，言則入六事矣。」

translations.literal: Ministers can only keep silent — if they speak, they fall under the six offenses."
translations.idiomatic: Officials can only keep quiet — speak and you violate one of the six prohibitions."

sentences.zh: 乃具論其情，改詔行之，於是上封者以千數。

translations.literal: He thereupon fully explained the situation; the edict was revised and promulgated — memorialists submitted by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He explained the problem in full. The edict was revised and issued, and memorials poured in by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 起光知陳州，過闕，留為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Guang was recalled to govern Chenzhou; passing the capital he was retained as Vice Director of the Department of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was recalled to govern Chenzhou, but passing the capital he was kept on as Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾自登州召還，緣道人相聚號呼曰：「寄謝司馬相公，毋去朝廷，厚自愛以活我。」

translations.literal: When Su Shi was recalled from Dengzhou, people along the road gathered and shouted: "Please tell Prime Minister Sima — do not leave the court; take good care of yourself to save us."
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was recalled from Dengzhou, people along the road gathered and shouted: "Tell Prime Minister Sima not to leave court — take care of yourself so you can save us."

sentences.zh: 是時天下之民，引領拭目以觀新政，而議者猶謂「三年無改于父之道」，但毛舉細事，稍塞人言。

translations.literal: At this time the people throughout the realm stretched their necks and wiped their eyes to watch the new policies, yet some ministers still cited "three years without altering the father's ways" — nitpicking petty matters and gradually choking off public speech.
translations.idiomatic: All across the empire people craned their necks and watched for the new policies. Yet some officials still invoked "three years without changing the father's ways," nitpicking minor points and slowly shutting down open debate.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「先帝之法，其善者雖百世不可變也。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Among the late Emperor's laws, those that are good cannot be altered even for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "Among the late Emperor's laws, what was good should stand for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 若安石、惠卿所建，為天下害者，改之當如救焚拯溺。

translations.literal: Those that Anshi and Huiqing established to the realm's harm must be changed as one would rescue from fire or drowning.
translations.idiomatic: What Anshi and Huiqing built to the empire's harm must be undone as urgently as saving someone from fire or drowning.

sentences.zh: 況太皇太后以母改子，非子改父。」

translations.literal: Moreover the Empress Dowager alters her son's policies as a mother — it is not a son altering his father's."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Empress Dowager is a mother correcting her son — not a son overturning his father's legacy."

sentences.zh: 眾議甫定。

translations.literal: The assembly's debate was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The debate was settled.

sentences.zh: 遂罷保甲團教，不復置保馬；

translations.literal: The community defense and militia training system was abolished, and the government horse program was not restored;
translations.idiomatic: The militia training system was abolished and the government horse program was not revived;

sentences.zh: 廢市易法，所儲物皆鬻之，不取息，除民所欠錢；

translations.literal: The market-control law was repealed — stored goods were all sold, no interest taken, and the people's outstanding debts cancelled;
translations.idiomatic: The market-control law was abolished. Stored goods were sold off, interest was waived, and the people's debts were forgiven;

sentences.zh: 京東鐵錢及茶鹽之法，皆復其舊。

translations.literal: The iron-coin, tea, and salt monopolies in the eastern capital region were all restored to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: The iron-coin, tea, and salt systems in the eastern capital region were all restored to their old forms.

sentences.zh: 或謂光曰：「熙、豐舊臣，多憸巧小人，他日有以父子義間上，則禍作矣。」

translations.literal: Some told Guang: "Many of the Xi and Feng era veterans are crafty petty men — one day they may use the bond between father and son to sow division with the sovereign, and disaster will follow."
translations.idiomatic: Some warned Guang: "Many holdovers from the Xi and Feng years are cunning petty men. One day they may drive a wedge between father and son with the throne, and trouble will follow."

sentences.zh: 光正色曰：「天若祚宗社，必無此事。」

translations.literal: Guang said sternly: "If Heaven blesses the altars of state, this will surely not happen."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said sternly: "If Heaven protects the dynasty, that will never happen."

sentences.zh: 於是天下釋然，曰：「此先帝本意也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the realm was reassured, saying: "This was the late Emperor's true intent."
translations.idiomatic: The empire was reassured at last, saying: "This was the late Emperor's true intent."

sentences.zh: 元祐元年復得疾，詔朝會再拜，勿舞蹈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou he fell ill again; an edict permitted him to bow twice at court audiences but not perform the full prostration dance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou he fell ill again. An edict allowed him to bow twice at court but exempted him from the full prostration dance.

sentences.zh: 時青苗、免役、將官之法猶在，而西戎之議未決。

translations.literal: At the time the Green Sprouts, Labor Exemption, and commander-reform laws still remained, and debate over the western barbarians was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Green Sprouts, Labor Exemption, and the commander-reform laws were still in place, and policy toward the western tribes remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 光歎曰：「四患未除，吾死不瞑目矣。」

translations.literal: Guang sighed: "Four afflictions are not yet removed — I cannot close my eyes in death."
translations.idiomatic: Guang sighed: "Four evils remain — I cannot die in peace."

sentences.zh: 折簡與呂公著云：「光以身付醫，以家事付愚子，惟國事未有所託，今以屬公。」

translations.literal: He sent a note to Lü Gongzhu saying: "Guang entrusts his person to physicians, his household affairs to his foolish son — only state affairs have no one to receive them; he now commits them to you."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a note to Lü Gongzhu: "I leave my body to the doctors and my household to my foolish son. State affairs alone have no one — I now entrust them to you."

sentences.zh: 乃論免役五害，乞直降敕罷之。

translations.literal: He thereupon laid out the five harms of the Labor Exemption law and petitioned that it be abolished by direct imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out the five harms of Labor Exemption and asked that it be abolished by direct imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 諸將兵皆隸州縣，軍政委守令通決。

translations.literal: All frontier troops were placed under prefectures and counties; military matters were left to prefects, magistrates, and vice-prefects to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops were placed under prefectures and counties, with military decisions left to prefects, magistrates, and vice-prefects.

sentences.zh: 廢提舉常平司，以其事歸之轉運、提點刑獄。

translations.literal: The Ever-Normal supervising commission was abolished and its duties returned to transport commissioners and judicial investigators.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal supervising commission was abolished and its work returned to transport commissioners and judicial investigators.

sentences.zh: 邊計以和戎為便。

translations.literal: Border strategy favored peace with the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Border policy favored peace with the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 謂監司多新進少年，務為刻急，令近臣於郡守中選舉，而於通判中舉轉運判官。

translations.literal: He said that too many circuit supervisors were newly promoted young men pursuing harsh severity — he ordered close ministers to select from among prefects, and from among vice-prefects to nominate transport vice-commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He said too many circuit supervisors were young newcomers obsessed with severity. He had close ministers choose from among prefects, and nominate transport vice-commissioners from among vice-prefects.

sentences.zh: 又立十科薦士法。

translations.literal: He also established the Ten Categories method of recommending scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He also instituted the Ten Categories system for recommending talent.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was approved.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎，免朝覲，許乘肩輿，三日一入省。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery — exempted from court audiences, permitted to ride in a sedan chair, and required to enter the Secretariat only once every three days.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, exempt from regular court attendance, allowed a sedan chair, and required to enter the Secretariat only once every three days.

sentences.zh: 光不敢當，曰：「不見君，不可以視事。」

translations.literal: Guang did not dare accept, saying: "Without seeing the sovereign, one cannot conduct affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Guang declined, saying: "Without seeing the ruler, I cannot govern."

sentences.zh: 詔令子康扶入對，且曰：「毋拜。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Kang to support him into audience, adding: "Do not bow."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his son Kang to help him into audience and added: "No bowing required."

sentences.zh: 遂罷青苗錢，復常平糶糴法。

translations.literal: Green Sprouts money was thereupon abolished and the Ever-Normal grain sale-and-purchase system restored.
translations.idiomatic: Green Sprouts lending was abolished and the Ever-Normal grain sale-and-purchase system restored.

sentences.zh: 兩宮虛己以聽。

translations.literal: Both palaces emptied themselves to listen to him.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Empress Dowager and the Emperor deferred to him completely.

sentences.zh: 遼、夏使至，必問光起居，敕其邊吏曰：「中國相司馬矣，毋輕生事、開邊隙。」

translations.literal: When Liao and Xia envoys arrived they invariably asked after Guang's health; they were instructed to tell their border officials: "The Middle Kingdom has made Sima its chancellor — do not lightly provoke trouble or open a border conflict."
translations.idiomatic: When Liao and Xia envoys arrived they always inquired after Guang. Their border officials were instructed: "The Song have made Sima chancellor — do not provoke trouble or open a border clash."

sentences.zh: 光自見言行計從，欲以身徇社稷，躬親庶務，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: Seeing that his words and deeds were followed in policy, Guang wished to devote his person to the altars of state — handling affairs in person, sparing neither day nor night.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his counsel followed in policy, Guang meant to give his life to the state — handling affairs himself, day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 賓客見其體羸，舉諸葛亮食少事煩以為戒，光曰：「死生，命也。」

translations.literal: Guests seeing how frail he had become cited Zhuge Liang's eating little yet burdened with many tasks as a warning; Guang said: "Life and death are fate."
translations.idiomatic: Visitors, seeing how thin he had grown, warned him with Zhuge Liang's example — eating little while burdened with endless work. Guang said: "Life and death are fate."

sentences.zh: 為之益力。

translations.literal: He applied himself all the more vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: He worked all the harder.

sentences.zh: 病革，不復自覺，諄諄如夢中語，然皆朝廷天下事也。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical he was no longer fully lucid — murmuring as in dream speech, yet all of it concerned court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned critical he was barely conscious, murmuring as in a dream — yet everything he said was about court and empire.

sentences.zh: 是年九月薨，年六十八。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month he died at sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year in the ninth month, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后聞之慟，與帝即臨其喪，明堂禮成不賀，贈太師、溫國公，襚以一品禮服，賻銀絹七千。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager mourned deeply on hearing it; she and the Emperor immediately attended his funeral; the Hall of Brightness ceremony was completed without celebration; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wen; vested with first-rank mourning garments; granted seven thousand taels of silver and silk in funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager grieved deeply on hearing the news. She and the Emperor went at once to his funeral. The Hall of Brightness rites were completed without celebration. He was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wen, dressed in first-rank mourning robes, and granted seven thousand taels of silver and silk in funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔戶部侍郎趙瞻、內侍省押班馮宗道護其喪，歸葬陝州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zhan and Palace Inner Service Commissioner Feng Zongdao to escort his funeral procession; he was buried in Shaan Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zhan and Palace Inner Service Commissioner Feng Zongdao to escort the funeral home. He was buried in Shaan Province.

sentences.zh: 諡曰「文正」，賜碑曰「忠清粹德」。

translations.literal: His posthumous epithet was "Cultured and Correct," and he was granted a stele inscribed "Loyal, Pure, and of Refined Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous epithet "Cultured and Correct," and a stele bearing the inscription "Loyal, Pure, and of Refined Virtue."

sentences.zh: 京師人罷市往弔，鬻衣以致奠，巷哭以過車。

translations.literal: People in the capital closed the markets to mourn him; they sold clothes to offer sacrifices and wept in the alleys as the funeral procession passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital people shut their shops to mourn him, sold garments to pay for offerings, and wept in the streets as the bier passed.

sentences.zh: 及葬，哭者如哭其私親。

translations.literal: At the burial the mourners wept as for their own kin.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial the mourners wept as though for their own kin.

sentences.zh: 嶺南封州父老，亦相率具祭，都中及四方皆畫像以祀，飲食必祝。

translations.literal: The elders of Fengzhou in Lingnan also came in groups to offer sacrifice; throughout the capital and in every region portraits were painted for worship, and at meals they always offered prayers.
translations.idiomatic: Elders in Fengzhou in the far south also gathered to offer sacrifice; in the capital and across the realm his portrait was painted for veneration, and at every meal people prayed to it.

sentences.zh: 光孝友忠信，恭儉正直，居處有法，動作有禮。

translations.literal: Guang was filial, friendly, loyal, and trustworthy, respectful, frugal, upright, and direct; in dwelling he had method, in movement he had ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was filial, loyal, and trustworthy, respectful, frugal, and upright; his household ran by rule and his every gesture observed ritual.

sentences.zh: 在洛時，每往夏縣展墓，必過其兄旦，旦年將八十，奉之如嚴父，保之如嬰兒。

translations.literal: While in Luoyang, whenever he went to Xia County to tend the tombs he always visited his elder brother Dan; Dan was nearly eighty, and Guang served him as to a stern father and guarded him as an infant.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang, whenever he went to Xia County to tend the family graves he always called on his elder brother Dan, who was nearly eighty; Guang served him as to a strict father and watched over him as over a child.

sentences.zh: 自少至老，語未嘗妄，自言：「吾無過人者，但平生所為，未嘗有不可對人言者耳。」

translations.literal: From youth to old age his words were never false; he said himself: "I have nothing surpassing others — only that in all I have done in life there has been nothing I could not face others with."
translations.idiomatic: From youth to age he never spoke falsely; he said: "I surpass no one — only that in everything I have done in life there is nothing I could not tell the world."

sentences.zh: 誠心自然，天下敬信，陝、洛間皆化其德，有不善，曰：「君實得無知之乎？」

translations.literal: His sincerity was natural; all under Heaven respected and trusted him; in Shaan and Luoyang all were transformed by his virtue — if one did wrong, people said: "Could Junshi not know of this?"
translations.idiomatic: His sincerity was innate; the empire trusted him. In Shaan and Luoyang his virtue transformed custom — if someone did wrong, people asked: "Would Junshi not know?"

sentences.zh: 光於物澹然無所好，於學無所不通，惟不喜釋、老，曰：「其微言不能出吾書，其誕吾不信也。」

translations.literal: Guang was indifferent to things and fond of nothing; in learning there was nothing he did not master — only he did not like Buddhism and Daoism, saying: "Their subtle words cannot go beyond our books; their extravagances I do not believe."
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for possessions and had no hobbies; in scholarship there was nothing he had not mastered — only he disliked Buddhism and Daoism, saying: "Their subtleties add nothing to our classics, and their fables I do not credit."

sentences.zh: 洛中有田三頃，喪妻，賣田以葬，惡衣菲食以終其身。

translations.literal: In Luoyang he had three qing of fields; when his wife died he sold the fields to bury her and wore coarse clothes and ate plain food to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He owned three qing of land in Luoyang; when his wife died he sold it for her burial and lived in coarse clothes and plain food for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，御史周秩首論光誣謗先帝，盡廢其法。

translations.literal: In the early Shaosheng era Investigating Censor Zhou Zhi was first to accuse Guang of slandering the late emperor and abolishing all his laws completely.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shaosheng reign Investigating Censor Zhou Zhi was first to charge that Guang had slandered the late emperor and that all his policies must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 章惇、蔡卞請發塚斫棺，帝不許，乃令奪贈諡，仆所立碑。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun and Cai Bian asked to open the tomb and break the coffin; the Emperor did not permit it, but ordered the posthumous gifts and epithet withdrawn and the stele he had erected thrown down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun and Cai Bian asked to open his tomb and smash his coffin; the Emperor refused, but ordered his posthumous honors withdrawn and the stele he had raised cast down.

sentences.zh: 而惇言不已，追貶清遠軍節度副使，又貶崖州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Yet Dun would not cease and pursued further demotion to military vice commissioner at Qingyuan, then to registrar of the household at Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dun would not relent and had him further demoted to military vice commissioner at Qingyuan, then to registrar of the household at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復太子太保。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne Guang was restored to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne he was restored to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 蔡京擅政，復降正議大夫，京撰《姦黨碑》，令郡國皆刻石。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing monopolized power he was again demoted to Regular Grandee of Discussion; Jing composed the Stele of Wicked Faction and ordered every commandery and county to carve it in stone.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing seized power he was demoted again to Regular Grandee of Discussion; Jing wrote the Stele of Wicked Faction and ordered every prefecture and county to carve it in stone.

sentences.zh: 長安石工安民當鐫字，辭曰：「民愚人，固不知立碑之意。

translations.literal: A stonemason of Chang'an named An Min was to cut the characters; he declined, saying: "I am a foolish man and do not know the meaning of erecting this stele.
translations.idiomatic: A Chang'an stonemason named An Min was assigned to cut the inscription; he refused: "I am only a common craftsman and do not understand why this stele is raised.

sentences.zh: 但如司馬相公者，海內稱其正直，今謂之奸邪，民不忍刻也。」

translations.literal: But one like Chancellor Sima is called upright throughout the realm — now to call him wicked, I cannot bear to carve it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chancellor Sima is hailed as upright throughout the empire — to call him wicked now is more than I can carve."

sentences.zh: 府官怒，欲加罪，泣曰：「被役不敢辭，乞免鐫安民二字于石末，恐得罪於後世。」

translations.literal: The prefectural officer was angry and would punish him; weeping he said: "I dare not refuse forced labor — only beg that my name An Min be omitted from the foot of the stone, lest I offend posterity."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect threatened punishment; weeping, he said: "I dare not refuse the work — only let my name An Min be left off the stone, lest posterity condemn me."

sentences.zh: 聞者愧之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard were ashamed.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，還贈諡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang his posthumous gifts and epithet were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang his posthumous honors were restored.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，配饗哲宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Jianyan era he was given a place in the temple sacrifices to Emperor Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianyan he was given a place in the temple sacrifices to Emperor Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 子 康

translations.literal: His son Kang
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang

sentences.zh: 康，字公休，幼端謹，不妄言笑，事父母至孝。

translations.literal: Kang, styled Gongxiu, was from childhood proper and cautious, never speaking or laughing rashly; in serving his parents he was utterly filial.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, whose courtesy name was Gongxiu, was from childhood grave and careful, never speaking or laughing lightly, and served his parents with the utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 敏學過人，博通群書，以明經上第。

translations.literal: Quick in learning beyond others, he mastered many books and passed the classics examination in the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: He learned faster than others, mastered many books, and passed the classics examination in the top rank.

sentences.zh: 光修《資治通鑒》，奏檢閱文字。

translations.literal: When Guang compiled the Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government he memorialized that Kang should collate the text.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang compiled the Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government he had Kang appointed to collate the text.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，勺飲不入口三日，毀幾滅性。

translations.literal: When his mother died he took not a spoonful for three days and was nearly destroyed by grief.
translations.idiomatic: Observing mourning for his mother, he took not a spoonful of food for three days and was nearly destroyed by grief.

sentences.zh: 光居洛，士之從學者退與康語，未嘗不有得。

translations.literal: When Guang lived in Luoyang, scholars who came to study would speak with Kang on leaving and always gained something.
translations.idiomatic: While Guang lived in Luoyang, scholars who came to study would speak with Kang afterward and always learned something.

sentences.zh: 塗之人見其容止，雖不識，皆知其為司馬氏子也。

translations.literal: Passersby who saw his bearing, though they did not know him, all knew he was a son of the Sima family.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers who saw his bearing, though strangers, all knew at once he was a son of the Sima house.

sentences.zh: 以韓絳薦，為秘書，由正字遷校書郎。

translations.literal: On Han Jiang's recommendation he became secretary; from proofreader he was promoted to collator.
translations.idiomatic: On Han Jiang's recommendation he entered the Secretariat; from proofreader he rose to collator.

sentences.zh: 光薨，治喪皆用《禮經》家法，不為世俗事。

translations.literal: When Guang died, Kang conducted the mourning entirely by the ritual codes in the Classics of Rites, with no worldly customs.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang died, Kang conducted the mourning wholly by the family rites in the Book of Rites, without worldly custom.

sentences.zh: 得遺恩，悉以與族人。

translations.literal: The grace gifts he received he gave entirely to his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The grace gifts he received he gave entirely to his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 服除，召為著作佐郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as assistant in the Bureau of Compilation with concurrent post as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as assistant in the Bureau of Compilation with a concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「比年以來，旱暵為虐，民多艱食。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "In recent years drought has been cruel and the people have often lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "In recent years drought has ravaged the land and the people have often gone hungry.

sentences.zh: 若復一不稔，則公私困竭，盜賊可乘。

translations.literal: If there is another poor harvest, public and private resources will be exhausted and bandits will have their chance.
translations.idiomatic: If harvest fails again, public and private stores will be drained and bandits will seize their chance.

sentences.zh: 自古聖賢之君，非無水旱，惟有以待之，則不為甚害。

translations.literal: Sage and worthy rulers of antiquity were not without flood and drought — only if one prepares against them they do not become grave harm.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers of old also knew flood and drought — but with preparation the harm need not be grave.

sentences.zh: 願及今秋熟，令州縣廣糴，民食所餘，悉歸於官。

translations.literal: I pray that while this autumn's harvest is still good, prefectures and counties may broadly purchase grain; whatever the people have left over should all go to the government stores.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that while this autumn's harvest is still ample, every prefecture and county buy grain broadly and place whatever the people can spare in government granaries.

sentences.zh: 今冬來春，令流民就食，候鄉里豐穰，乃還本土。

translations.literal: This winter and spring let the displaced take food where they can; wait until the countryside is abundant, then send them home.
translations.idiomatic: This winter and spring let refugees eat where they can; when the countryside recovers, send them home.

sentences.zh: 凡為國者，一絲一毫皆當愛惜，惟於濟民則不宜吝。

translations.literal: Whoever governs the state must cherish every thread and hair — only in relieving the people should one not be stingy.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever governs a state must treasure every thread and hair — only in saving the people should one not be sparing.

sentences.zh: 誠能捐數十萬金帛，以為天下大本，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: If you can truly give several hundred thousand in gold and silk for the great foundation of the realm, all under Heaven will be greatly blessed."
translations.idiomatic: If the court can truly spend several hundred thousand in gold and silk for the realm's foundation, the empire will be greatly blessed."

sentences.zh: 拜右正言，以親嫌未就職。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrator but because of kinship did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Remonstrator but declined because of kinship restrictions.

sentences.zh: 為哲宗言前世治少亂多，祖宗創業之艱難，積累之勤勞，勸帝及時向學，守天下大器，且勸太皇太后每于禁中訓迪，其言切至。

translations.literal: He spoke to Zhezong on how in past ages order was brief and disorder long, the hardship of the founders' enterprise, the diligence of accumulated effort — urging the Emperor to study in good time, guard the great vessel of the realm, and also urging the Grand Empress Dowager to instruct him daily in the inner palace; his words were cutting and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhezong how in past ages good order was brief and disorder long, how hard the founders' work had been and how much diligence it had cost — urging the Emperor to study while there was time, guard the great vessel of the realm, and urging the Grand Empress Dowager to instruct him daily in the inner palace; his words were urgent and thorough.

sentences.zh: 邇英進講，又言：「《孟子》於書最醇正，陳王道尤明白，所宜觀覽。」

translations.literal: In lecture at the Hall for Cultivating Virtue he also said: "Mencius among books is most pure and correct, and states the royal way most clearly — it is fit for Your Majesty's reading."
translations.idiomatic: In lecture at the Hall for Cultivating Virtue he said: "Of all books Mencius is purest and states the royal way most clearly — Your Majesty should read it."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「方讀其書」。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I am now reading that book."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I am reading that book now."

sentences.zh: 尋詔講官節以進。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered the lecturers to abridge the text as they advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered the lecturers to present the text in abridged sections.

sentences.zh: 康自居父喪，居廬疏食，寢於地，遂得腹疾，至是不能朝謁。

translations.literal: Since his father's death Kang had lived in a mourning hut on plain food, sleeping on the ground, and thus contracted abdominal illness so that he could no longer attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Since his father's death Kang had lived in a mourning hut on plain food, sleeping on the ground, and developed abdominal illness so severe he could no longer attend court.

sentences.zh: 賜優告。

translations.literal: He was granted extended leave.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted extended leave.

sentences.zh: 疾且殆，猶具疏所當言者以待，曰：「得一見天子極言而死無恨。」

translations.literal: As his illness grew grave he still prepared memorials on what ought to be said, saying: "If I could see the Son of Heaven once and speak my utmost I would die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he still drafted memorials on what must be said, declaring: "If I could see the Son of Heaven once and speak my fill, I would die content."

sentences.zh: 使召醫李積於兗。

translations.literal: He sent for the physician Li Ji of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent for the physician Li Ji of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 積老矣，鄉民聞之，往告曰：「百姓受司馬公恩深，今其子病，願速往也。」

translations.literal: Ji was old; the villagers hearing of it went to tell him: "The people owe Chancellor Sima deep kindness — now his son is ill; go quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Ji was old; when villagers heard, they told him: "The people owe Chancellor Sima deep kindness — now his son is ill; go at once."

sentences.zh: 來者日夜不絕，積遂行；

translations.literal: Visitors came day and night without cease, and Ji set out;
translations.idiomatic: Visitors came day and night without cease, and Ji set out;

sentences.zh: 至，則不可為矣。

translations.literal: when he arrived, nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: when he arrived, nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 年四十一而卒。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-one.

sentences.zh: 公卿嗟痛于朝，士大夫相弔于家，市井之人，無不哀之。

translations.literal: Chief ministers lamented at court, scholar-officials mourned at his home, and among market folk all grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers grieved at court, scholar-officials mourned at his home, and in the markets none failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 詔贈右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed him Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 康為人廉潔，口不言財。

translations.literal: Kang was incorruptible in person and never spoke of wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was personally incorruptible and never spoke of money.

sentences.zh: 初，光立神道碑，帝遣使賜白金二千兩，康以費皆官給，辭不受。

translations.literal: Initially when Guang erected his spirit-way stele the Emperor sent two thousand taels of white silver; Kang held that all expenses were supplied by the state and declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang erected his spirit-way stele the Emperor sent two thousand taels of white silver; Kang held that all costs were met by the state and refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遣家吏如京師納之，乃止。

translations.literal: He sent a household steward to the capital to return it, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a household steward to the capital to return it, and only then was the matter closed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：熙寧新法病民，海內騷動，忠言讜論，沮抑不行；

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The New Policies of the Xining era afflicted the people; the realm was in turmoil; loyal and forthright words were suppressed and not carried out;
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The New Policies of the Xining era harmed the people; the realm was in turmoil; loyal counsel was suppressed;

sentences.zh: 正人端士，擯棄不用。

translations.literal: Upright men and gentlemen were cast aside and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men were cast aside and not employed.

sentences.zh: 聚斂之臣日進，民被其虐者將二十年。

translations.literal: Men of exaction advanced daily; the people suffered under their cruelty for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Men of exaction advanced daily; the people suffered their cruelty for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 方是時，光退居於洛，若將終身焉。

translations.literal: At that time Guang retired to Luoyang as if he would live out his life there.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guang retired to Luoyang as though he would never leave.

sentences.zh: 而世之賢人君子，以及庸夫愚婦，日夕引領望其為相，至或號呼道路，願其毋去朝廷，是豈以區區材智所能得此于人人哉？

translations.literal: Yet worthy gentlemen of the age, and even common men and foolish women, day and night stretched their necks hoping he would become chief minister — some even cried in the roads, begging him not to leave the court — could mere talent and wisdom win such devotion from everyone?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the worthy, and even common men and foolish women, day and night looked to him as chief minister — some cried in the roads begging him to stay — could talent alone win such love from all?

sentences.zh: 德之盛而誠之著也。

translations.literal: It was the fullness of his virtue and the manifestness of his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: It was the greatness of his virtue and the manifest sincerity of his heart.

sentences.zh: 一旦起而為政，毅然以天下自任，開言路，進賢才。

translations.literal: Once he rose to govern, he boldly took the realm upon himself, opened the avenue of speech, and advanced worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took power he boldly shouldered the realm, opened the avenue of speech, and advanced the worthy.

sentences.zh: 凡新法之為民害者，次第取而更張之，不數月之間，剗革略盡。

translations.literal: Every New Policy that harmed the people he abolished in turn; within a few months they were largely swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Every New Policy that harmed the people he struck down in turn; within months they were largely gone.

sentences.zh: 海內之民，如寒極而春，旱極而雨，如解倒懸，如脫桎梏，如出之水火之中也。

translations.literal: The people of the realm were like those long frozen who feel spring, long parched who feel rain — like men released from hanging upside down, freed from fetters, rescued from flood and fire.
translations.idiomatic: The people were like those long frozen who feel spring, long parched who feel rain — like men cut down from the rack, freed from chains, pulled from flood and fire.

sentences.zh: 相與咨嗟歎息，歡欣鼓舞，甚若更生，一變而為嘉祐、治平之治。

translations.literal: They sighed and rejoiced together as if born anew; in an instant the rule of Jiayou and Zhiping returned.
translations.idiomatic: They sighed and rejoiced as if born anew; in an instant the rule of Jiayou and Zhiping seemed restored.

sentences.zh: 君子稱其有旋乾轉坤之功，而光於是亦老且病矣。

translations.literal: Gentlemen praised his power to turn heaven and earth; yet by then Guang was old and ill.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen praised his power to turn the age; yet by then Guang was old and ill.

sentences.zh: 天若祚宋，慭遺一老，則奸邪之勢未遽張，紹述之說未遽行，元祐之臣固無恙也。

translations.literal: If Heaven had blessed Song and left one old man, the power of the wicked would not have risen so fast, the doctrine of succession would not have spread so soon, and the men of Yuanyou would have remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven had blessed Song and left one old man standing, villainy would not have risen so fast, the doctrine of succession would not have spread, and the men of Yuanyou would have been safe.

sentences.zh: 人眾能勝天，靖康之變，或者其可少緩乎？

translations.literal: When the many overcome heaven — might the Jingkang disaster have been somewhat delayed?
translations.idiomatic: When the multitude overpowers heaven — might the Jingkang catastrophe have come later?

sentences.zh: 借曰有之，當不至如是其酷也。

translations.literal: Even if it came, it need not have been so cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Even if it came, it need not have been so savage.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「哲人云亡，邦國殄瘁。」

translations.literal: The Odes says: "When the wise man perishes, the state is laid waste."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "When the wise man perishes, the state is laid waste."

sentences.zh: 嗚呼悲夫！

translations.literal: Alas, how tragic!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how tragic!

sentences.zh: 康濟美象賢，不幸短命而死，世尤惜之。

translations.literal: Kang inherited his father's excellence and resembled the worthy, yet died young — the age grieved for him especially.
translations.idiomatic: Kang inherited his father's excellence and seemed born for greatness, yet died young — the age grieved for him all the more.

sentences.zh: 然康不死，亦將不免於紹聖之禍矣。

translations.literal: Yet if Kang had not died, he too would not have escaped the disasters of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yet had Kang lived, he too would not have escaped the Shaosheng persecutions.

sentences.zh: 呂公著

translations.literal: Lu Gongzhu
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gongzhu

sentences.zh: 呂公著，字晦叔，幼嗜學，至忘寢食。

translations.literal: Lu Gongzhu, styled Huishu, loved learning from childhood to the point of forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gongzhu, whose courtesy name was Huishu, loved learning from childhood to the point of forgetting sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 父夷簡器異之，曰：「他日必為公輔。」

translations.literal: His father Yijian regarded him as extraordinary and said: "One day he will be chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yijian saw his promise and said: "One day he will be chief minister."

sentences.zh: 恩補奉禮郎，登進士第，召試館職，不就。

translations.literal: By grace he was made Gentleman for Ceremonial Observance, passed the jinshi examination, and was summoned to test for an academy post but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: By grace he was made Gentleman for Ceremonial Observance, passed the jinshi examination, and was summoned to test for an academy post but declined.

sentences.zh: 通判潁州，郡守歐陽修與為講學之友。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Yingzhou the prefect Ouyang Xiu became his friend in classical study.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of Yingzhou he studied the classics with the prefect Ouyang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 後修使契丹，契丹主問中國學行之士，首以公著對。

translations.literal: Later when Xiu went as envoy to the Khitan, the Khitan ruler asked which men in China were most learned and virtuous; Xiu named Gongzhu first.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu later went as envoy to the Khitan, the Khitan ruler asked which Chinese men were most learned and virtuous; Xiu named Gongzhu first.

sentences.zh: 判吏部南曹，仁宗獎其恬退，賜五品服。

translations.literal: He judged the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel; Renzong praised his quiet withdrawal and granted fifth-rank dress.
translations.idiomatic: He judged the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel; Renzong praised his quiet withdrawal and granted him fifth-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 除崇文院檢討、同判太常寺。

translations.literal: He was made collator in the Hall of Literature and concurrent judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made collator in the Hall of Literature and concurrent judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 壽星觀營真宗神御殿，公著言：「先帝已有三種御，而建立不已，殆非祀無豐昵之義。」

translations.literal: At the Longevity Star Observatory they were building a hall for the spirit tablet of Emperor Zhenzong; Gongzhu said: "The late emperor already has three spirit halls, yet building continues without end — this is hardly the meaning of sacrifices that do not favor the near."
translations.idiomatic: At the Longevity Star Observatory they built a hall for Emperor Zhenzong's spirit tablet; Gongzhu objected: "The late emperor already has three spirit halls, yet building continues — this is hardly the rite that does not favor the near."

sentences.zh: 進知制誥，三辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was promoted to drafter of edicts but thrice declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of edicts but three times declined.

sentences.zh: 改天章閣待制兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns with concurrent post as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns with a concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 英宗親政，加龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: When Yingzong personally took power, [Gongzhu] was made academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong personally took power, Gongzhu was made academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 方議追崇濮王，或欲稱皇伯考，公著曰：「此真宗所以稱太祖，豈可施于王。」

translations.literal: Just then they were debating posthumous honors for the Prince of Pu; some wished to call him Imperial Uncle-Father. Gongzhu said: "This is why Emperor Zhenzong called Emperor Taizu as he did — how can it be applied to a prince?"
translations.idiomatic: As they debated posthumous honors for the Prince of Pu, some wished to call him Imperial Uncle-Father. Gongzhu said, "This is why Emperor Zhenzong styled Emperor Taizu as he did — how can that be applied to a prince?"

sentences.zh: 及下詔稱親，且班諱，又言：「稱親則有二父之嫌，王諱但可避於上前，不應與七廟同諱。」

translations.literal: When an edict was issued calling him "kin" and taboo names were promulgated, he again said: "Calling him kin creates the suspicion of two fathers; the prince's taboo names may be avoided only before the throne — they should not share taboo with the seven temples."
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called him kin and taboo names were promulgated, he said again, "Calling him kin creates the suspicion of two fathers; the prince's taboo names may be avoided only before the throne and should not share taboo with the seven temples."

sentences.zh: 呂誨等坐論濮王去，公著言：「陛下即位以來，納諫之風未彰，而屢絀言者，何以風示天下？」

translations.literal: When Lü Hui and others were punished for debating the Prince of Pu and removed, Gongzhu said: "Since Your Majesty took the throne the spirit of accepting remonstrance has not been displayed, yet those who speak are repeatedly silenced — how will this instruct the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Hui and others were punished for debating the Prince of Pu and removed, Gongzhu said, "Since Your Majesty took the throne the spirit of accepting remonstrance has not been shown, yet those who speak are repeatedly silenced — how will this instruct the realm?"

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂乞補外，帝曰：「學士朕所重，其可以去朝廷？」

translations.literal: He thereupon asked to fill an outside post. The Emperor said: "The academician is one I value — how can he leave the court?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked for an outside appointment. The Emperor said, "The academician is one I value — how can he leave the court?"

sentences.zh: 請不已，出知蔡州。

translations.literal: He pleaded without cease and was sent out as prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded without cease and was sent out as prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，召為翰林學士、知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne he was summoned as Hanlin Academician and director of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne he was summoned as Hanlin Academician and director of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace.

sentences.zh: 司馬光以論事罷中丞，還經幄。

translations.literal: When Sima Guang was dismissed as investigating censor for his remonstrance he returned to the inner lecture service.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang was dismissed as investigating censor for remonstrating he returned to the inner lecture service.

sentences.zh: 公著封還其命曰：「光以舉職賜罷，是為有言責者不得盡其言也。」

translations.literal: Gongzhu returned the appointment sealed, saying: "Guang was dismissed for performing his duty — this means men with a duty to speak cannot speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu returned the sealed appointment, saying: "Guang was dismissed for doing his duty — so men charged to speak cannot speak fully."

sentences.zh: 詔以告直付閣門。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the report sent to the Palace Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the report sent to the Palace Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 公著又言：「制命不由門下，則封駁之職，因臣而廢。

translations.literal: Gongzhu again said: "If imperial commands do not pass through the Secretariat, the duty of seal and rebuke is voided because of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu said again: "If imperial commands bypass the Secretariat, the duty of seal and rebuke is voided by a subject's act.

sentences.zh: 願理臣之罪，以正紀綱。」

translations.literal: I pray that my offense be judged to set right the statutes."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that my offense be judged to restore the statutes."

sentences.zh: 帝諭之曰：「所以徙光者，賴其勸學耳，非以言事故也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed him: "The reason Guang was moved is that we rely on him to encourage learning — not because of his words."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him: "Guang was moved because we rely on him to encourage learning — not because of his remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 公著請不已，竟解銀臺司。

translations.literal: Gongzhu pleaded without cease and in the end was relieved of the Silver Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu pleaded without cease and in the end was relieved of the Silver Terrace.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，知開封府。

translations.literal: In the early Xining era he was made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xining era he was made prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時夏秋淫雨，京師地震。

translations.literal: At the time summer and autumn had excessive rain and the capital was shaken by earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: That summer and autumn brought excessive rain and the capital was shaken by earthquake.

sentences.zh: 公著上疏曰：「自昔人君遇災者，或恐懼以致福，或簡誣以致禍。

translations.literal: Gongzhu submitted a memorial: "From of old when rulers met disasters, some through fear attained blessing, some through levity incurred calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu memorialized: "From of old when rulers met disaster, some through fear won blessing, some through levity brought calamity.

sentences.zh: 上以至誠待下，則下思盡誠以應之，上下至誠而變異不消者，未之有也。

translations.literal: If the ruler treats those below with utmost sincerity, those below will think to repay with utmost sincerity — never yet has sincerity above and below failed to dispel strange occurrences.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler treats those below with utmost sincerity, those below will repay with utmost sincerity — never yet has such sincerity failed to dispel strange portents.

sentences.zh: 惟君人者去偏聽獨任之弊，而不主先入之語，則不為邪說所亂。

translations.literal: Only if a ruler removes the fault of partial listening and sole reliance, and does not give primacy to words heard first, will he not be confused by perverse talk.
translations.idiomatic: Only if a ruler avoids listening to one side alone and relying on one man alone, and does not treat prior impressions as decisive, will he not be thrown into confusion by wicked counsel.

sentences.zh: 顏淵問為邦，孔子以遠佞人為戒。

translations.literal: When Yan Yuan asked about governing a state, Confucius warned him to keep flatterers far off.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Yuan asked how to govern a state, Confucius warned him to keep flatterers at a distance.

sentences.zh: 蓋佞人惟恐不合於君，則其勢易親；

translations.literal: For flatterers fear only that they will not please the ruler — thus their position tends easily toward closeness;
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers fear only that they will not please the ruler, so their position tends easily toward intimacy;

sentences.zh: 正人惟恐不合於義，則其勢易疏。

translations.literal: upright men fear only that they will not accord with righteousness — thus their position tends easily toward distance.
translations.idiomatic: upright men fear only that they will not accord with what is right, so their position tends easily toward distance.

sentences.zh: 惟先格王正厥事，未有事正而世不治者也。」

translations.literal: Only when the king first rectifies affairs will the world be governed — never has there been rectification of affairs without order under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Only when the king first sets affairs right is the world governed — never yet has right conduct in affairs failed to bring order to the realm."

sentences.zh: 禮官用唐故事，請以五月御大慶殿受朝，因上尊號。

translations.literal: The ritual officials, following Tang precedent, requested that in the fifth month he hold court at the Grand Celebration Hall and thereby receive a honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Following Tang precedent, the ritual officials asked that in the fifth month the emperor hold court at the Grand Celebration Hall and there accept a honorific title.

sentences.zh: 公著曰：「陛下方度越漢、唐，追復三代，何必于陰長之日，為非禮之會，受無益之名？」

translations.literal: Gongzhu said: "Your Majesty now surpasses Han and Tang and seeks to restore the Three Dynasties — why must it be on a day when yin grows long, at an unorthodox assembly, to receive a title of no benefit?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu said: "Your Majesty already surpasses Han and Tang and seeks to restore the ways of the Three Dynasties — why gather on a day of lengthening yin at an irregular rite only to receive a title that brings no benefit?"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The Emperor] followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 二年，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時王安石方行青苗法，公著極言曰：「自古有為之君，未有失人心而能圖治，亦未有能脅之以威、勝之以辯而能得人心者也。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Anshi was implementing the Green Sprouts law. Gongzhu spoke at length: "From of old among active rulers, none who lost the people's hearts could plan for order; nor has anyone ever won hearts by threatening with awe or prevailing in argument.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Anshi was putting the Green Sprouts system into effect, Gongzhu spoke forcefully: "Never in history has an active ruler lost the people's hearts and still brought order; nor has anyone ever won hearts by threatening them or prevailing in debate.

sentences.zh: 昔日之所謂賢者，今皆以此舉為非，而生議者一切祗為流俗浮論，豈昔皆賢而今皆不肖乎？」

translations.literal: Those called worthy in former days all regard this measure as wrong; yet dissenters are all dismissed as vulgar floating talk — were they all worthy then and all unworthy now?"
translations.idiomatic: Men once called worthy all regard this measure as wrong, yet every objecting voice is dismissed as shallow popular chatter — were they all worthy then and all unworthy now?"

sentences.zh: 安石怒其深切。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi was angered by the depth of his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was enraged by how forcefully he spoke.

sentences.zh: 帝使舉呂惠卿為御史，公著曰：「惠卿固有才，然奸邪不可用。」

translations.literal: The Emperor had Lu Huiqing recommended as investigating censor. Gongzhu said: "Huiqing indeed has talent, but he is treacherous and wicked and cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor sought to recommend Lu Huiqing as investigating censor, Gongzhu said: "Huiqing has talent, but he is treacherous and cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 帝以語安石，安石益怒，誣以惡語，出知潁州。

translations.literal: The Emperor told Wang Anshi; Anshi grew angrier still, slandered him with harsh words, and had him sent out as prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Wang Anshi, who grew still angrier, slandered Gongzhu with vicious charges, and had him sent out as prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，彗星見，詔求直言。

translations.literal: In the eighth year a comet appeared; an edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year a comet appeared, and an edict called for frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 公著上疏曰：「陛下臨朝願治，為日已久，而左右前後，莫敢正言。

translations.literal: Gongzhu submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has sat on the throne desiring order for a long time, yet among those at your left and right, before and behind, none dare speak straight.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu memorialized: "Your Majesty has long sat on the throne wishing to govern well, yet among those around you none dare speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 使陛下有欲治之心，而無致治之實，此任事之臣負陛下也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty has a heart that wishes for order but lacks the reality of bringing order, this is the fault of the ministers who bear responsibility — they have failed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty has the will to govern but not the reality of good government, the ministers charged with affairs have failed you.

sentences.zh: 夫士之邪正、賢不肖，既素定矣。

translations.literal: Whether gentlemen are crooked or straight, worthy or unworthy, is by nature already settled.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a gentleman is upright or corrupt, worthy or unworthy, is by nature already clear.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，前日所舉，以為天下之至賢；

translations.literal: Now it is not so: those raised up yesterday were deemed the worthiest under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Now it is otherwise: those promoted yesterday were called the worthiest in the realm;

sentences.zh: 而後日逐之，以為天下至不肖。

translations.literal: yet those driven off the next day are deemed the most unworthy under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: yet those cast out the next day are called the most unworthy in the realm.

sentences.zh: 其于人材既反覆不常，則於政事亦乖戾不審矣。

translations.literal: If judgment of men is thus changeable, then in governance affairs will also be erratic and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When judgment of men shifts so constantly, governance too becomes erratic and uncertain.

sentences.zh: 古之為政，初不信於民者有之，若子產治鄭，一年而人怨之，三年而人歌之。

translations.literal: In ancient governance there were cases not trusted at first by the people — as when Zichan governed Zheng: in one year the people resented him, in three years they sang his praise.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times some rulers were not trusted at first — Zichan governing Zheng was resented after one year yet praised in song after three.

sentences.zh: 陛下垂拱仰成，七年於此，然輿人之誦，亦未有異于前日，陛下獨不察乎？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ruled with folded hands relying on ministers' accomplishments — seven years have passed — yet what common men chant has not differed from former days. Does Your Majesty alone not observe this?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ruled at ease for seven years, yet what common folk say has scarcely changed. Does Your Majesty not see this?"

sentences.zh: 起知河陽，召還，提舉中太一宮，遷翰林學士承旨，改端明殿學士、知審官院。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Heyang, then summoned back, made superintendent of the Central Grand Unity Palace, promoted to chief Hanlin Academician, and changed to academician of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Heyang, then recalled, made superintendent of the Central Grand Unity Palace, promoted to chief Hanlin Academician, and appointed academician of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 帝從容與論治道，遂及釋、老，公著問曰：「堯、舜知此道乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor at leisure discussed the way of governance with him and came to Buddhism and Daoism. Gongzhu asked: "Did Yao and Shun know this way?"
translations.idiomatic: In an unhurried conversation about governance the Emperor turned to Buddhism and Daoism. Gongzhu asked: "Did Yao and Shun know this doctrine?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「堯、舜豈不知？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Would Yao and Shun not have known?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Surely Yao and Shun knew it?"

sentences.zh: 公著曰：「堯、舜雖如此，而惟以知人安民為難，所以為堯、舜也。」

translations.literal: Gongzhu said: "Though Yao and Shun were so, they regarded knowing men and settling the people as the hard things — that is why they were Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu said: "Even Yao and Shun were so, yet they held knowing men and settling the people to be the hard part — that is what made them Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 帝又言唐太宗能以權智御臣下。

translations.literal: The Emperor also said that Emperor Taizong of Tang could control his ministers by resourceful wit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor added that Emperor Taizong of Tang could control his ministers through shrewd wit.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「太宗之德，以能屈己從諫爾。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Taizong's virtue lay merely in being able to humble himself and follow remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Taizong's virtue lay in his ability to humble himself and heed remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 未幾，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Before long he became vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 有欲復肉刑者，議取死囚試劓、刖，公著曰：「試之不死，則肉刑遂行矣。」

translations.literal: Some wished to restore corporal mutilation and proposed trying nose-cutting and foot-cutting on condemned prisoners. Gongzhu said: "If the trial does not end in death, then corporal mutilation will forthwith be practiced."
translations.idiomatic: When some wished to restore corporal punishments and proposed testing nose-cutting and foot-amputation on condemned prisoners, Gongzhu said: "If the test subjects do not die, corporal punishment will be put into practice."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 夏人幽其主，將大舉討之。

translations.literal: The Tangut people imprisoned their ruler; [the court] was about to mount a major punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut people had imprisoned their ruler, and the court prepared a major punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 公著曰：「問罪之師，當先擇帥，苟未得人，不如勿舉。」

translations.literal: Gongzhu said: "An army sent to demand accountability must first choose its commander — if the right man is not found, better not launch it."
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu said: "A punitive army must first have the right commander — if no suitable man is found, it is better not to act."

sentences.zh: 及兵興，秦、晉民力大困，大臣不敢言，公著數白其害。

translations.literal: When war began, the people of Qin and Jin were greatly exhausted; great ministers dared not speak, but Gongzhu several times reported the harm.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out the people of Qin and Jin were sorely strained; senior ministers dared not speak, but Gongzhu repeatedly reported the damage.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，以疾丐去位，除資政殿學士、定州安撫使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, on grounds of illness he sought to leave office; he was made academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance and pacification commissioner of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he asked to leave office because of illness and was made academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance and pacification commissioner of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄永樂城陷，帝臨朝歎曰：「邊民疲弊如此，獨呂公著為朕言之耳。」

translations.literal: Soon Yongle fortress fell. At court the Emperor sighed: "The border people are worn and exhausted to this degree — only Lu Gongzhu has spoken of it to me."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the fortress at Yongle fell. At court the Emperor sighed: "The border people are this badly worn — only Lu Gongzhu has told me."

sentences.zh: 徙揚州，加大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yangzhou and given the grand academician title.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yangzhou and promoted to grand academician.

sentences.zh: 將立太子，帝謂輔臣，當以呂公著、司馬光為師傅。

translations.literal: When a crown prince was to be installed, the Emperor told his chief ministers that Lu Gongzhu and Sima Guang should serve as his tutors.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was to be installed, the Emperor told his chief ministers that Lu Gongzhu and Sima Guang should be his tutors.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，以侍讀還朝。

translations.literal: When Zhezong took the throne, [Gongzhu] returned to court from his lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong took the throne, Gongzhu returned to court from his lectureship.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后遣使迎，問所欲言，公著曰：「先帝本意，以寬省民力爲先。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager sent envoys to welcome him and asked what he wished to say. Gongzhu said: "The late emperor's original intent was to put easing and sparing the people's strength first.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager sent envoys to welcome him and asked what he wished to say. Gongzhu said, "The late emperor's original intent was to ease the people's burdens first.

sentences.zh: 而建議者以變法侵民爲務，與己異者一切斥去，故日久而弊愈深，法行而民愈困。

translations.literal: Yet those who proposed policy made encroaching on the people through reform their task, and all who differed from them were cast out; thus as days lengthened abuses grew deeper, and though laws were enforced the people grew more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who proposed policy made encroaching on the people through reform their task, and all who differed were cast out; so as time passed abuses deepened and though laws were enforced the people grew more distressed.

sentences.zh: 誠得中正之士，講求天下利病，協力而爲之，宜不難矣。」

translations.literal: If truly upright men were obtained to examine the realm's ills and benefits and work together, it should not be hard."
translations.idiomatic: If truly upright men were found to examine the realm's ills and benefits and work together, it should not be hard."

sentences.zh: 至則上言曰：「人君初即位，當正始以示天下，修德以安百姓。

translations.literal: On arrival he submitted a memorial: "When a ruler first takes the throne he should begin rightly to show the realm and cultivate virtue to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he memorialized: "When a ruler first takes the throne he should begin rightly to show the realm and cultivate virtue to settle the people.

sentences.zh: 修德之要，莫先於學。

translations.literal: The key to cultivating virtue is none before learning.
translations.idiomatic: The key to cultivating virtue is learning above all.

sentences.zh: 學有緝熙于光明，則日新以底至治者，學之力也。

translations.literal: When learning illumines and brightens, daily renewal reaches perfect order — that is learning's power.
translations.idiomatic: When learning illumines and brightens, daily renewal reaches perfect order — that is learning's power.

sentences.zh: 謹昧死陳十事，曰畏天、愛民、修身、講學、任賢、納諫、薄斂、省刑、去奢、無逸。」

translations.literal: I humbly risk death to present ten matters: revering Heaven, loving the people, cultivating the person, promoting learning, employing the worthy, accepting remonstrance, lightening levies, reducing punishments, discarding extravagance, and avoiding idleness."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly risk death to present ten matters: revering Heaven, loving the people, cultivating the person, promoting learning, employing the worthy, accepting remonstrance, lightening levies, reducing punishments, discarding extravagance, and avoiding idleness."

sentences.zh: 又乞備置諫員，以開言路。

translations.literal: He also asked that remonstrance officials be fully appointed to open the path of speech.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that remonstrance officials be fully appointed to open the path of frank speech.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書左丞、門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，拜尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou he was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Grand Counselor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou he was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Grand Counselor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三省並建，中書獨為取旨之地。

translations.literal: With all three departments operating jointly, the Secretariat alone was the place for obtaining imperial decisions.
translations.idiomatic: With all three departments active together, the Secretariat alone remained the place where imperial decisions were taken.

sentences.zh: 乃請事於三省者，與執政同進呈，取旨而各行之。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested that matters belonging to all three departments be jointly presented with the chief ministers, decisions taken, and each department execute them separately.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that business belonging to all three departments be presented jointly with the chief ministers, decisions taken, and each department carry them out on its own.

sentences.zh: 又執政官率數日一聚政事堂，事多決於其長，同列莫得預。

translations.literal: Again, chief ministers had generally gathered at the Hall of Affairs only every few days; matters were mostly decided by the senior man and fellow appointees could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers had also been meeting at the Hall of Affairs only every few days; most matters were decided by the senior minister and the others were left out.

sentences.zh: 至是，始命日集，遂為定制。

translations.literal: From this time he ordered daily assembly — it thereafter became fixed practice.
translations.idiomatic: From this point daily meetings were mandated, and the practice became permanent.

sentences.zh: 與司馬光同心輔政，推本先帝之志，凡欲革而未暇與革而未定者，一一舉行之。

translations.literal: Together with Sima Guang he assisted in governance with one heart, tracing back to the late emperor's intent; every reform wished for but not yet undertaken, or begun but unsettled, was carried through one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Working in concert with Sima Guang, he traced policy back to the late emperor's intent and carried through, one by one, every reform that had been planned but deferred or begun but left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 民歡呼鼓舞，咸以為便。

translations.literal: The people shouted and danced for joy; all regarded it as beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: The people shouted and danced for joy; all regarded the changes as a clear benefit.

sentences.zh: 光薨，獨當國，除吏皆一時之選。

translations.literal: When Guang died, [Gongzhu] alone bore the burden of state; every appointment was a man chosen for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: After Guang died he bore the burden of state alone and filled every post with men chosen for the moment.

sentences.zh: 時科舉罷詞賦，專用王安石經義，且雜以釋氏之說。

translations.literal: At the time the examinations had abolished rhyme-prose and relied solely on Wang Anshi's commentaries on the classics, mixed moreover with Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations had dropped rhyme-prose and relied solely on Wang Anshi's commentaries on the classics, often mixed with Buddhist ideas.

sentences.zh: 凡士子自一語上，非新義不得用，學者至不誦正經，唯竊安石之書以干進，精熟者轉上第，故科舉益弊。

translations.literal: From a single phrase upward, candidates had to follow the new interpretation or could not pass; scholars even ceased reciting the orthodox classics and only cribbed Wang's books to seek advancement — those who mastered them rose to top ranks, and thus the examinations grew ever more corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: From the first phrase upward, nothing but the new interpretation would do; scholars stopped reciting the orthodox classics and merely cribbed Wang's books to advance, with the most practiced winning top ranks — so the examinations grew ever more corrupt.

sentences.zh: 公著始令禁主司不得出題老、莊書，舉子不得以申、韓、佛書為學，經義參用古今諸儒說，毋得專取王氏。

translations.literal: Gongzhu first ordered that chief examiners must not set questions from the Laozi and Zhuangzi; candidates might not take Shen Buhai, Han Fei, or Buddhist texts as their learning; commentary on the classics should draw on ancients and moderns among all Confucian schools and must not rely exclusively on the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu ordered that examiners no longer set questions from the Laozi and Zhuangzi, that candidates not study Shenzi, Han Feizi, or Buddhist works, that commentary draw on all schools of Confucian learning past and present, and that Wang Anshi's interpretation not be the sole standard.

sentences.zh: 復賢良方正科。

translations.literal: He restored the examination for the worthy, upright, and square.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Worthy and Upright examination.

sentences.zh: 右司諫賈易以言事訐直詆大臣，將峻責，公著以為言，止罷知懷州。

translations.literal: Right remonstrance official Jia Yi, for his blunt remonstrance slandering great ministers, was to be sternly punished; Gongzhu spoke on his behalf, and the punishment was reduced to dismissal as prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Jia Yi was to be severely punished for bluntly attacking senior ministers; Gongzhu spoke for him, and the sentence was reduced to dismissal as prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 退謂同列曰：「諫官所論，得失未足言。

translations.literal: Retiring he told his colleagues: "What the remonstrance official argued — its right and wrong scarcely need be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told his colleagues: "Right or wrong, what the remonstrance official said is not the point.

sentences.zh: 顧主上春秋方盛，慮異時有進諛說惑亂者，正賴左右爭臣耳，不可豫使人主輕厭言者也。」
