translations.literal: But the sovereign is in the prime of life; we must fear that in time flatterers will advance and confuse him — we rely on contentious ministers at hand; one must not beforehand cause the ruler lightly to weary of speech."
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is still young; we must worry that someday flatterers will confuse him — we depend on contentious ministers at his side, and we must not teach the ruler to grow weary of frank speech."

sentences.zh: 眾莫不歎服。

translations.literal: None present failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: All present sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃首領鬼章青宜結久為洮、河患，聞朝廷弭兵省戍，陰與夏人合謀復取熙、岷。

translations.literal: The Tibetan leader Qingtang Jiaoshi had long plagued Tao and He; hearing that the court had ceased campaigns and reduced garrisons, he secretly joined the Tangut in plotting to retake Xi and Min.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan leader Qingtang Jiaoshi had long troubled the Tao and He region; learning that the court had halted campaigns and reduced garrisons, he secretly plotted with the Tangut to retake Xi and Min.

sentences.zh: 公著白遣軍器丞游師雄以便宜諭諸將，不逾月，生致于闕下。

translations.literal: Gongzhu reported and dispatched armory vice director You Shixiong with discretionary authority to instruct the generals; within a month [Qingtang] was captured alive and brought to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu sent armory vice director You Shixiong with discretionary authority to instruct the generals; within a month Qingtang was captured alive and brought to court.

sentences.zh: 帝宴近臣於資善堂，出所書唐人詩分賜。

translations.literal: The Emperor feasted close ministers at the Hall for Cultivation of Virtue and distributed Tang poems he had copied.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor entertained close ministers at the Hall for Cultivation of Virtue and handed out Tang poems he had copied.

sentences.zh: 公著乃集所講書要語明白、切於治道者，凡百篇進之，以備遊意翰墨，為聖學之助。

translations.literal: Gongzhu thereupon collected essential passages from books he had lectured on — clear and relevant to governance — one hundred pieces in all, and presented them to accompany his leisure in brush and ink and aid the sage's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu collected a hundred essential passages from books he had taught — clear and useful for governance — and presented them so the emperor's leisure in brushwork might also serve his learning.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，懇辭位，拜司空、同平章軍國事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he earnestly declined office and was appointed Grand Mentor and co-administrator of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he earnestly declined office and was appointed Grand Mentor and co-administrator of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 宋興以來，宰相以三公平章重事者四人，而公著與父居其二，士豔其榮。

translations.literal: Since the founding of Song, only four chief ministers had held a Three Dukes' rank while administering state affairs; Gongzhu and his father accounted for two — scholars admired the glory.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the Song, only four chief ministers had held a Three Dukes' rank while administering state affairs; Gongzhu and his father accounted for two, and scholars admired the distinction.

sentences.zh: 詔建第於東府之南，啟北扉，以便執政會議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a residence built south of the Eastern Secretariat, with a northern gate opened for the convenience of chief ministers' councils.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a residence built south of the Eastern Secretariat with a north gate opened so the chief ministers could meet conveniently.

sentences.zh: 凡三省、樞密院之職，皆得總理。

translations.literal: He might oversee in general the duties of all three departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was empowered to oversee in general the duties of all three departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 間日一朝，因至都堂，其出不以時，蓋異禮也。

translations.literal: On alternate days he attended court; he also came to the metropolitan hall — his comings and goings not confined to regular hours: an extraordinary honor.
translations.idiomatic: He attended court every other day and also came to the metropolitan hall; his comings and goings were not bound by regular hours — an extraordinary privilege.

sentences.zh: 明年二月薨，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后見輔臣泣曰：「邦國不幸，司馬相公既亡，呂司空復逝。」

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager, seeing the chief ministers, wept: "The state is unfortunate — Chancellor Sima is already gone, and Grand Mentor Lu has again passed away."
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Empress Dowager saw the chief ministers she wept: "The state is unfortunate — Chancellor Sima is gone and Grand Mentor Lu has followed him."

sentences.zh: 痛閔久之。

translations.literal: She grieved long in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: She mourned at length.

sentences.zh: 帝亦悲感，即詣其家臨奠，賜金帛萬。

translations.literal: The Emperor too was moved to grief; he went at once to his home to offer condolences and bestowed ten thousand in gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor too was grieved; he went at once to mourn at his home and bestowed ten thousand strings of cash in gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 贈太師、申國公，諡曰「正獻」，御筆碑首曰「純誠厚德」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Shen; his posthumous title was "Correct Presentation"; the imperial brush on his stele read "Pure Sincerity and Deep Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Shen, with the posthumous title "Correct Presentation"; the emperor's own brush on his stele read "Pure Sincerity and Deep Virtue."

sentences.zh: 公著自少講學，即以治心養性為本，平居無疾言遽色，於聲利紛華，泊然無所好。

translations.literal: From youth Gongzhu lectured on learning, taking cultivation of heart and nourishing of nature as foundation; in daily life he had no harsh words or sudden changes of countenance; toward rank and gain, splendor and display, he was tranquil and without attachment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he lectured on learning with self-cultivation as the foundation; in daily life he never spoke harshly or showed sudden anger; toward rank, gain, and worldly splendor he was utterly detached.

sentences.zh: 暑不揮扇，寒不親火，簡重清靜，蓋天稟然。

translations.literal: In summer he did not wield a fan; in cold he did not draw near the fire — grave, restrained, clear and quiet: this was his innate endowment.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he did not use a fan; in winter he did not sit by the fire — grave, restrained, and serene by innate temperament.

sentences.zh: 其識慮深敏，量閎而學粹，遇事善決，苟便於國，不以私利害動其心。

translations.literal: His insight was deep and quick, his capacity broad and learning pure; meeting affairs he decided well; if it served the state he would not let private gain or harm move his heart.
translations.idiomatic: His insight was deep and quick, his breadth of mind wide and his learning pure; in affairs he decided well, and if something served the state private interest would not sway him.

sentences.zh: 與人交，出於至誠，好德樂善，見士大夫以人物為意者，必問其所知與其所聞，參互考實，以達於上。

translations.literal: In dealing with others he acted from utmost sincerity; he loved virtue and delighted in good; seeing scholar-officials mindful of men's qualities, he always asked what they knew and what they had heard, cross-checking to verify and conveying it upward.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt with others in utmost sincerity, loved virtue and delighted in talent; when he met scholar-officials who cared about men's character he asked what they knew and had heard, cross-checked the accounts, and passed the results upward.

sentences.zh: 每議政事，博取眾善以為善，至所當守，則毅然不回奪。

translations.literal: Whenever he discussed governance he gathered all that was good and made it his own; yet where he must stand firm, he was resolute and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: In deliberating policy he drew together every sound view, yet on what he had to uphold he stood firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗言其于人材不欺，如權衡之稱物。

translations.literal: Shenzong once said that in judging men he did not deceive, like a steelyard weighing things.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong once said that in judging men he never deceived, like a balance weighing things true.

sentences.zh: 尤能避遠聲跡，不以知人自處。

translations.literal: He was especially able to keep aloof from reputation and trace and did not present himself as one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially adept at keeping his reputation quiet and did not parade his talent for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 始與王安石善，安石兄事之，安石博辯騁辭，人莫敢與亢，公著獨以精識約言服之。

translations.literal: At first he was on good terms with Wang Anshi; Anshi treated him as an elder brother. Anshi was broad in debate and rushed forth in rhetoric; no one dared contend with him — Gongzhu alone subdued him with refined insight and restrained speech.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Anshi began as friends; Anshi treated him as an elder brother. Anshi was a forceful debater and no one dared stand up to him, yet Gongzhu alone won him over with refined insight and measured words.

sentences.zh: 安石嘗曰：「疵吝每不自勝，一詣長者，即廢然而反，所謂使人之意消者，于晦叔見之。」

translations.literal: Anshi once said: "My faults and stinginess — I often cannot master them myself; once I visit an elder, I at once wilt and return — what is called making another's intent fade away, I find in Huishu."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi once said: "My faults and pettiness often overcome me; one visit to an elder and I wilt and turn back — that power to dissolve another's anger, I find in Huishu."

sentences.zh: 又謂人曰：「晦叔為相，吾輩可以言仕矣。」

translations.literal: He also told others: "When Huishu becomes chief minister, we may speak of taking office."
translations.idiomatic: He also told others: "When Huishu becomes chief minister, we may speak of serving in office again."

sentences.zh: 後安石得志，意其必助己，而數用公議，列其過失，以故交情不終。

translations.literal: Later when Anshi got his way he expected Gongzhu would surely aid him, but [Gongzhu] repeatedly invoked public opinion and listed his faults — thus their friendship did not last.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Anshi came to power he expected Gongzhu would help him, but Gongzhu repeatedly voiced public opinion and listed his faults, and their friendship ended.

sentences.zh: 于講說尤精，語約而理盡。

translations.literal: In lecturing he was especially refined; his words were spare yet principles complete.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching he was especially masterful; his words were spare yet his principles fully delivered.

sentences.zh: 司馬光曰：「每聞晦叔講，便覺己語為煩。」

translations.literal: Sima Guang said: "Whenever I hear Huishu lecture, I feel my own words become tedious."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said: "Whenever I hear Huishu lecture, my own speech begins to feel wordy."

sentences.zh: 其為名流所敬如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he honored by leading men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which leading men held him.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，章惇爲相，以翟思、張商英、周秩居言路，論公著更熙、豐法度，削贈諡，毀所賜碑，再貶建武軍節度副使、昌化軍司戸參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, Zhang Dun became chief minister; Zhai Si, Zhang Shangying, and Zhou Zhi held the path of speech. They charged that Gongzhu had altered the Xining and Yuanfeng institutions, stripped his posthumous gifts and epithet, destroyed the stele he had been granted, and again demoted him to military vice commissioner of Jianwu Army and registrar of the household of Changhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaosheng, Zhang Dun became chief minister and placed Zhai Si, Zhang Shangying, and Zhou Zhi on the remonstrance path. They charged that Gongzhu had altered the Xining and Yuanfeng institutions, stripped his posthumous honors, destroyed the stele he had been granted, and again demoted him to military vice commissioner of Jianwu Army and registrar of the household of Changhua Army.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，追復太子太保。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, [Gongzhu] was posthumously restored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, Gongzhu was posthumously restored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 蔡京擅政，復降左光祿大夫，入黨籍，尋復銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing monopolized power, [Gongzhu] was again demoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, entered the partisan register, and soon was restored to Silver-Green Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing monopolized power, Gongzhu was again demoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, entered the partisan register, and soon was restored to Silver-Green Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，悉還贈諡。

translations.literal: Early in the Shaoxing era all posthumous gifts and the epithet were fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era all posthumous honors were fully restored.

sentences.zh: 子希哲、希純。

translations.literal: His sons were Xizhe and Xi Chun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xizhe and Xi Chun.

sentences.zh: 希哲，字原明，少從焦千之、孫復、石介、胡瑗學，復從程顥、程頤、張載遊，聞見由是益廣。

translations.literal: Xizhe, styled Yuanming, in youth studied under Jiao Ganzhi, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, and Hu Yuan; later associated with Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Zhang Zai, and his hearing and seeing thereby grew broader.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe, whose courtesy name was Yuanming, studied in youth under Jiao Ganzhi, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, and Hu Yuan, and later learned from Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Zhang Zai, so his horizons broadened.

sentences.zh: 以蔭入官，父友王安石勸其勿事科舉，以僥倖利祿，遂絕意進取。

translations.literal: Entering office by yin privilege, his father's friend Wang Anshi urged him not to pursue the examinations, lest he seek rank and emolument by luck — he thereupon abandoned thought of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through yin privilege; his father's friend Wang Anshi urged him not to sit for the examinations lest he chase office by luck, and he gave up any thought of advancement.

sentences.zh: 安石為政，將置其子雱於講官，以希哲有賢名，欲先用之。

translations.literal: When Anshi held power he planned to place his son Pang among lecturers; because Xizhe had a reputation for worth he wished to use him first.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi came to power he planned to place his son Pang among the lecturers; because Xizhe had a reputation for worth he wished to promote him first.

sentences.zh: 希哲辭曰：「辱公相知久，萬一從仕，將不免異同，則疇昔相與之意盡矣。」

translations.literal: Xizhe declined: "I have long been honored by your knowing me; if I should take office, differences will be unavoidable, and the meaning of our former mutual regard will be utterly lost."
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe declined: "You have known me graciously for so long; if I take office we will surely disagree, and everything we once shared will be lost."

sentences.zh: 安石乃止。

translations.literal: Anshi thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi desisted.

sentences.zh: 公著作相，二弟已官省寺，希哲獨滯管庫，久乃判登聞鼓院，力辭。

translations.literal: When Gongzhu became chief minister, his two younger brothers already held posts in the central ministries; Xizhe alone remained stuck in warehouse management — long afterward he was assigned to judge the Palace Gate Drum Court and strenuously declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzhu became chief minister his two younger brothers already held posts in the central ministries, while Xizhe alone languished in warehouse duties; only much later was he assigned to the Palace Gate Drum Court, which he strenuously declined.

sentences.zh: 公著歎曰：「當世善士，吾收拾略盡，爾獨以吾故置不試，命也夫！」

translations.literal: Gongzhu sighed: "Among worthy men of the age I have gathered nearly all — you alone, because of me, are set aside without trial — this is fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu sighed: "I have gathered nearly every worthy man of the age; you alone, because of me, are left untested — fate, alas!"

sentences.zh: 希哲母賢明有法度，聞公著言，笑曰：「是亦未知其子矣。」

translations.literal: Xizhe's mother was wise, clear, and observant of measure; hearing Gongzhu's words she laughed: "This too shows he does not yet know his son."
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe's mother was wise and disciplined; hearing this she laughed: "He does not know his son yet after all."

sentences.zh: 終公著喪，始為兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Only after Gongzhu's mourning ended did he become vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Only after his father's mourning ended did he become vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 范祖禹，其妹婿也，言于哲宗曰：「希哲經術操行，宜備勸講，其父常稱為不欺暗室。

translations.literal: Fan Zuyu, his brother-in-law, spoke to Zhezong: "Xizhe's classical learning and conduct qualify him to serve in admonition and lecture; his father often called him one who would not cheat even in an unlit room.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zuyu, who had married his sister, told Zhezong: "Xizhe's learning and conduct suit him for lecturing and remonstrance; his father often said he would not cheat even in an unlit room.

sentences.zh: 臣以婦兄之故，不敢稱薦，今方將引去，竊謂無嫌。」

translations.literal: Your servant, because of the tie through my wife's brother, dared not recommend him; now that I am about to withdraw, I believe there is no conflict of interest."
translations.idiomatic: As his brother-in-law I did not dare recommend him before; now that I am about to leave office I believe there is no conflict."

sentences.zh: 詔以為崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him lecturer at the Hall for Exaltation of Governance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him lecturer at the Hall for Exaltation of Governance.

sentences.zh: 其勸導人主以修身為本，修身以正心誠意為主。

translations.literal: In admonishing and guiding the sovereign he took self-cultivation as root, and self-cultivation took rectifying the heart and making intent sincere as chief matters.
translations.idiomatic: In advising the ruler he took self-cultivation as the foundation, and within self-cultivation he emphasized rectifying the mind and making intent sincere.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「心正意誠，則身修而天下化。

translations.literal: He said: "When heart is correct and intent sincere, the person is cultivated and all under Heaven is transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "When the mind is correct and intent sincere, the person is cultivated and the world is transformed.

sentences.zh: 若身不能修，雖左右之人且不能諭，況天下乎？」

translations.literal: If the person cannot be cultivated, even those beside one cannot be instructed — how much less all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot cultivate yourself, you cannot even instruct those beside you — how much less govern the world?"

sentences.zh: 擢右司諫，辭，未聽，私語祖禹曰：「若不得請，當以楊畏、來之邵為首。」

translations.literal: Promoted to right remonstrance official, he declined; [the court] did not heed him. Privately he told Fan Zuyu: "If my request is not granted, Yang Wei and Lai Zhishao should be placed at the head."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to right remonstrance official, he declined; the court would not listen. Privately he told Fan Zuyu: "If my request is denied, Yang Wei and Lai Zhishao should be placed at the head."

sentences.zh: 既而不拜。

translations.literal: And in the end he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 會紹聖黨論起，御史劉拯論其進不由科第，以秘閣校理知懷州。

translations.literal: Just as the partisan strife of Shaosheng arose, investigating censor Liu Cheng argued that his advancement did not come through the examinations; he was made collator in the Secret Archive and prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shaosheng factional strife erupted, investigating censor Liu Cheng argued that his advancement had not come through the examinations; he was made collator in the Secret Archive and prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人林希又言：「呂大防由公著援引，故進希哲以酬私恩。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat drafter Lin Xi also said: "Lu Dafang was promoted through Gongzhu's recommendation; therefore Xizhe was advanced to repay a private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Central Secretariat drafter Lin Xi also said: "Lu Dafang was promoted through Gongzhu's recommendation, so Xizhe was advanced to repay a private favor.

sentences.zh: 凡大防輩欺君賣國，皆公著為之倡；

translations.literal: All the crimes of Dafang's faction in deceiving the ruler and betraying the state were initiated by Gongzhu;
translations.idiomatic: All the crimes of Dafang's faction in deceiving the ruler and betraying the state were initiated by Gongzhu;

sentences.zh: 而公著之惡，則希哲導成之，豈宜汙華職。」

translations.literal: and the evil of Gongzhu was shaped under Xizhe's guidance — how could he be allowed to stain an exalted office?"
translations.idiomatic: and the evil of Gongzhu was shaped under Xizhe's guidance — how could he be allowed to stain an exalted office?"

sentences.zh: 於是但守本秩，俄分司南京，居和州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he kept only his original rank; soon he was assigned to the Nanjing branch office and lived in Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he kept only his original rank; soon he was assigned to the Nanjing branch office and lived in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，召為秘書少監，或以為太峻，改光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huizong's reign he was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat; some thought the post too lofty and he was changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huizong's reign he was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat; some thought the post too lofty, and he was changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 希哲力請外，以直秘閣知曹州。

translations.literal: Xizhe strongly requested an outside post and was made prefect of Caozhou with the rank of collator in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe strongly requested an outside post and was made prefect of Caozhou with the rank of collator in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 旋遭崇寧黨禍，奪職知相州，徙邢州。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered the factional disaster of Chongning, was stripped of office and made prefect of Xiangzhou, then transferred to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he suffered the factional disaster of Chongning, was stripped of office and made prefect of Xiangzhou, then transferred to Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 罷為宮祠。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to a sinecure temple post.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to a sinecure temple post.

sentences.zh: 羈寓淮、泗間，十餘年卒。

translations.literal: Living in exile between the Huai and Si rivers, he died after more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Living in exile between the Huai and Si rivers, he died after more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 希哲樂易簡儉，有至行，晚年名益重，遠近皆師尊之。

translations.literal: Xizhe was cheerful, easy, simple, and frugal, with supreme conduct; in later years his reputation grew ever weightier and men near and far all honored him as a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe was cheerful, easy, simple, and frugal, with supreme conduct; in later years his reputation grew ever weightier, and men near and far honored him as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 子：好問，有傳。

translations.literal: His son: Haowen, has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Haowen has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 子 希純

translations.literal: His son Xi Chun
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi Chun

sentences.zh: 希純，字子進，登第，為太常博士。

translations.literal: Xi Chun, styled Zijin, passed the examinations and became a doctorate in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chun, whose courtesy name was Zijin, passed the examinations and became a doctorate in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元祐祀明堂，將用皇祐故事，並饗天地百神，皆以祖宗配。

translations.literal: In Yuanyou, when sacrificing at the Bright Hall, the court planned to follow the Huangyou precedent of jointly feasting Heaven, Earth, and the hundred spirits, all with ancestral accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou, when sacrificing at the Bright Hall, the court planned to follow the Huangyou precedent of jointly feasting Heaven, Earth, and the hundred spirits, all with ancestral accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 希純言：「皇祐之禮，事不經見，嘉祐既已厘正。

translations.literal: Xi Chun said: "The Huangyou rite is a matter not established in precedent; in Jiayou it was already corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chun said: "The Huangyou rite lacks established precedent; in Jiayou it was already corrected.

sentences.zh: 至元豐中，但以英宗配上帝，悉罷從祀群神，得嚴父之義，請循其式。」

translations.literal: By Yuanfeng only Emperor Yingzong was paired with the Supreme Lord and all attendant sacrifices to the host of spirits were abolished — gaining the meaning of honoring the father; I pray we follow that form."
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanfeng only Emperor Yingzong was paired with the Supreme Lord and all attendant sacrifices to the host of spirits were abolished, honoring the father as ritual requires; I pray we follow that form."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 歷宗正、太常、秘書丞。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice director in the Court of the Imperial Clan, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice director in the Court of the Imperial Clan, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 哲宗議納后，希純請考三代昏禮，參祖宗之制，博訪令族，參求德配。

translations.literal: When Zhezong deliberated taking an empress, Xi Chun asked that the marriage rites of the Three Dynasties be examined, ancestral institutions consulted, prominent clans widely sought, and a worthy match sought.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong deliberated taking an empress, Xi Chun asked that the marriage rites of the Three Dynasties be examined, ancestral institutions consulted, prominent clans widely sought, and a worthy match found.

sentences.zh: 凡世俗所謂勘婚之書，淺陋不經，且一切屏絕，以防附會。

translations.literal: All vulgar so-called books for inspecting marriage are shallow, crude, and unorthodox — let them all be excluded to guard against forced correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: All vulgar so-called books for inspecting marriage are shallow, crude, and unorthodox; let them all be excluded to guard against forced matches.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎，以父諱不拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to drafting secretary but, because of taboo on his father's personal name, declined to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to drafting secretary but, because of taboo on his father's personal name, declined to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 擢起居舍人，權太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to court diarist and acting vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to court diarist and acting vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宣仁太后崩，希純慮奸人乘間進說搖主聽，即上疏曰：「自元祐初年，太皇聽斷，所用之人皆宿有時望，所行之事皆人所願行。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanren died, Xi Chun feared villainous men would seize the interval to advance arguments and sway the ruler's hearing; he at once submitted a memorial: "Since the early Yuanyou years the Grand Empress held judgment; the men she used all had long-standing public standing; the affairs she carried out were all what people wished done.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xuanren died, Xi Chun feared villainous men would seize the moment to sway the ruler; he at once memorialized: "Since early Yuanyou the Grand Empress held judgment; the men she used all had long-standing public standing, and the affairs she carried out were what people wished done.

sentences.zh: 唯是過惡得罪之徒，日伺變故，捭闔規利，今必以更改神宗法度為說。

translations.literal: Only those who had erred and been punished watch daily for change, scheming for advantage; they will surely speak now of altering Shenzong's institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who had erred and been punished watch daily for change, scheming for advantage; they will surely speak now of altering Shenzong's institutions.

sentences.zh: 臣以為先帝之功烈，萬世莫掩。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the late emperor's achievements can never be concealed for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that the late emperor's achievements can never be concealed for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 間有數事，為小人所誤，勢雖頗有損益，在於聖德，固無所虧。

translations.literal: A few matters were misled by petty men; though in effect there was some loss and gain, to his sacred virtue nothing was truly diminished.
translations.idiomatic: A few matters were misled by petty men; though in effect there was some loss and gain, to his sacred virtue nothing was truly diminished.

sentences.zh: 且英宗、神宗何嘗不改真宗、仁宗之政，亦豈盡用慶祖、太宗之法乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, did Emperors Yingzong and Shenzong not also alter the policies of Zhenzong and Renzong — and did they fully use the methods of Qingzu and Taizong?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, did Emperors Yingzong and Shenzong not also alter the policies of Zhenzong and Renzong — and did they fully adhere to the methods of the founding ancestors and Taizong?

sentences.zh: 小人既誤先帝，復欲誤陛下，不可不察。」

translations.literal: Petty men already misled the late emperor; they wish again to mislead Your Majesty — this cannot go unexamined."
translations.idiomatic: Petty men already misled the late emperor; they wish again to mislead Your Majesty — this cannot go unexamined."

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜中書舍人、同修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed central Secretariat drafter and co-compiler of national history.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed central Secretariat drafter and co-compiler of national history.

sentences.zh: 內侍梁從政、劉惟簡除內省押班，希純以親政之始，首錄二人，無以示天下，持不行。

translations.literal: Palace attendants Liang Congzheng and Liu Weijian were appointed inner-circuit wardens; Xi Chun, because this was the start of personal rule, held that installing these two men first offered no model to the realm, steadfastly refused to issue the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants Liang Congzheng and Liu Weijian were appointed inner-circuit wardens; Xi Chun, because this was the start of personal rule, held that installing these two men first offered no model to the realm and steadfastly refused to issue the edicts.

sentences.zh: 由是閹寺側目，或於庭中指以相示曰：「此繳還二押班詞頭者也。」

translations.literal: Hence the eunuchs glared; some in the courtyard would point and say to one another: "This is the one who returned the drafts for the two wardens' appointments."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the eunuchs glared; some in the courtyard would point and say to one another: "This is the one who returned the drafts for the two wardens' appointments."

sentences.zh: 章惇既相，出為寶文閣待制、知亳州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun became chief minister, [Xi Chun] was sent out as Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Literary Glory and prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun became chief minister, Xi Chun was sent out as Hanlin Academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Literary Glory and prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官張商英憾希純，攻之力。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Zhang Shangying resented Xi Chun and attacked him forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Zhang Shangying resented Xi Chun and attacked him forcefully.

sentences.zh: 又以外親嫌，連徙睦州、歸州。

translations.literal: Again, on grounds of affinity by marriage, he was transferred in succession to Muzhou and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Again, on grounds of affinity by marriage, he was transferred in succession to Muzhou and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 自京東而之浙西，自浙西而上三峽，名為易地，實困之也。

translations.literal: From the eastern capital region to western Zhe, from western Zhe up the Three Gorges — nominally a change of post, in reality an exhausting persecution.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern capital region to western Zhe, from western Zhe up the Three Gorges — nominally a change of post, in reality an exhausting persecution.

sentences.zh: 公著追貶，希純亦以屯田員外郎分司南京，居金州。

translations.literal: When Gongzhu was posthumously demoted, Xi Chun too was made vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture assigned to the Nanjing branch, living in Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzhu was posthumously demoted, Xi Chun too was made vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture assigned to the Nanjing branch, living in Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 又責舒州團練副使，道州安置。

translations.literal: He was further demoted to deputy military commissioner of Shuzhou and settled in Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted to deputy military commissioner of Shuzhou and settled in Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，還為待制、知瀛州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo he was restored as awaiting-order academician and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo he was restored as awaiting-order academician and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗聞其名，數稱之。

translations.literal: Huizong heard his name and praised him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong heard his name and praised him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 曾布忌希純，因其請覲，未及見，亟以邊，遽趣遣之。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu envied Xi Chun; when he requested an audience, before he could be received Zeng Bu hurried to the frontier and pressed for his immediate dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu envied Xi Chun; when he requested an audience, before he could be received Zeng Bu hurried to the frontier and pressed for his immediate dispatch.

sentences.zh: 俄改潁州，入崇寧黨籍。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Yingzhou and entered the Chongning faction list.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was changed to Yingzhou and entered the Chongning faction list.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 論曰：公著父子俱位至宰相，俱以司空平章軍國事，雖漢之韋、平，唐之蘇、李，榮盛孰加焉。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Gongzhu father and son both reached the chancellorship, both as Grand Mentor administering state affairs — even the Wei and Ping of Han, the Su and Li of Tang — what glory surpasses this?
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Gongzhu father and son both reached the chancellorship, both as Grand Mentor administering state affairs — even the Wei and Ping of Han, the Su and Li of Tang — what glory surpasses this?

sentences.zh: 夷簡多智數，公著則一切持正，以應天下之務，嗚呼賢哉。

translations.literal: Yijian was full of schemes; Gongzhu held uniformly to correctness in meeting the affairs of the realm — alas, how worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Yijian was full of schemes; Gongzhu held uniformly to correctness in meeting the affairs of the realm — alas, how worthy!

sentences.zh: 其論人才，如權衡之稱物，故一時賢士，收拾略盡。

translations.literal: In judging talent he was like a balance weighing things — thus worthy men of the age were nearly all gathered in.
translations.idiomatic: In judging talent he was like a balance weighing things true — thus worthy men of the age were nearly all gathered in.

sentences.zh: 司馬光疾甚，諄諄焉以國事為托，當時廷臣，莫公著若也審矣。

translations.literal: When Sima Guang was gravely ill he earnestly entrusted state affairs — among court ministers at the time, none was trusted like Gongzhu; this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang was gravely ill he earnestly entrusted state affairs to him — among court ministers at the time, none was trusted like Gongzhu; this is clear.

sentences.zh: 追考其平生事業，蓋守成之良相也。

translations.literal: Reviewing his life's work, he was essentially a fine minister for preserving an established order.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing his life's work, he was essentially a fine minister for preserving an established order.

sentences.zh: 然知子之賢而不能薦，殆猶未免於避嫌，而有愧于從祖云。

translations.literal: Yet knowing his son's worth and unable to recommend him — he perhaps could not escape the taint of avoiding suspicion, and had reason to feel ashamed before his collateral ancestor, one might say.
translations.idiomatic: Yet knowing his son's worth and unable to recommend him — he perhaps could not escape the taint of avoiding suspicion, and had reason to feel ashamed before his collateral ancestor, one might say.

sentences.zh: 希哲、希純世濟其美，然皆隱于崇寧党禍，何君子之不幸歟！

translations.literal: Xizhe and Xi Chun carried on his excellence through generations, yet both were lost in the Chongning faction disaster — how unfortunate for gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe and Xi Chun carried on his excellence through generations, yet both were lost in the Chongning faction disaster — how unfortunate for gentlemen!
